title.zh: 卷三十二 蜀書二 先主傳
title.en: Volume 32: Book of Shu 2 - Biography of the Former Lord
title.raw: 卷三十二 蜀書二 先主傳 Volume 32: Book of Shu 2 - Biography of the Former Lord

sentences.zh: 先主 劉備

translations.literal: The Former Lord Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord: Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 先主姓劉，諱備，字玄德，涿郡涿縣人，漢景帝子中山靖王勝之後也。

translations.literal: The Former Lord’s surname was Liu, his taboo name was Bei, his courtesy name Xuande; he was a man of Zhuo County in Zhuo Commandery; he was a descendant of Prince Jing of Zhongshan Sheng, son of Han Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord was Liu Bei, courtesy Xuande, from Zhuo county in Zhuo commandery, a descendant of Han Prince Jing of Zhongshan, Prince Sheng, son of Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 勝子貞，元狩六年封涿縣陸城亭侯，坐酎金失侯，因家焉。

translations.literal: Sheng’s son Zhen, in the sixth year of Yuanshou, was enfeoffed village marquis of Lucheng in Zhuo County; he sat guilty of ritual gold and lost the marquisate; therefore the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng’s son Liu Zhen received the village fief of Lucheng at Zhuo in the sixth year of Yuanshou, lost his rank over the “ritual gold” affair, and the line then made its home there.

sentences.zh: 〈典略曰：備本臨邑侯枝屬也。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Compendium says: Bei was originally a cadet branch of the marquis of Linyi.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Compendium states that Liu Bei sprang from a collateral branch of the marquises of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 先主祖雄，父弘，世仕州郡。

translations.literal: The Former Lord’s grandfather was Xiong, his father was Hong; for generations they served in prefecture and commandery offices.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu Xiong and father Liu Hong had for generations held posts in local government.

sentences.zh: 雄舉孝廉，官至東郡範令。

translations.literal: Xiong was recommended as filial and incorrupt; his office reached magistrate of Fan in Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong rose as a filial and incorrupt candidate to magistrate of Fan in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 先主少孤，與母販履織蓆為業。

translations.literal: The Former Lord in youth was orphaned; with his mother he sold shoes and wove mats for a living.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he and his mother earned their bread by selling straw sandals and weaving rush mats.

sentences.zh: 舍東南角籬上有桑樹生高五丈餘，遙望見童童如小車蓋，往來者皆怪此樹非凡，或謂當出貴人。

translations.literal: On the southeast corner fence of the house there was a mulberry tree grown more than five zhang high; looking from afar one saw it thick like a small carriage umbrella; comers and goers all marveled that this tree was not ordinary; some said there ought to emerge an eminent person.
translations.idiomatic: A mulberry by their southeast fence towered over five zhang, its canopy spreading like a carriage awning. Passersby called it uncanny and whispered that the house would rear a man of destiny.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：涿人李定雲：「此家必出貴人。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Springs and Autumns of Han and Jin says: a man of Zhuo, Li Ding, said: “This household will certainly produce an eminent person.”〉
translations.idiomatic: The Springs and Autumns of Han and Jin quotes a Zhuo townsman, Li Ding: “That roof will shelter greatness.”

sentences.zh: 先主少時，與宗中諸小兒於樹下戲，言：「吾必當乘此羽葆蓋車。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord was young, with the various children of the clan he played under the tree, saying: “I must someday ride this feather-canopy-covered carriage.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he played under that tree with his kinsmen’s children and declared, “One day I shall ride in the imperial feather-canopy carriage.”

sentences.zh: 」叔父子敬謂曰：「汝勿妄語，滅吾門也！

translations.literal: ” His uncle’s son Zijing said to him: “You must not speak recklessly—it will destroy our gate!
translations.idiomatic: ” His uncle Liu Zijing warned him, “Hush such talk, or you will bring the whole clan to ruin!”

sentences.zh: 」年十五，母使行學，與同宗劉德然、遼西公孫瓚俱事故九江太守同郡盧植。

translations.literal: ” At age fifteen, his mother sent him to pursue studies; together with clansman Liu Deran and Gongsun Zan of Liaoxi he served under former grand administrator of Jiujiang, Lu Zhi of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: ” At fifteen his mother sent him to school with his kinsman Liu Deran and Gongsun Zan of Liaoxi, all pupils of Lu Zhi, the former grand administrator of Jiujiang and a fellow townsman.

sentences.zh: 德然父元起常資給先主，與德然等。

translations.literal: Deran’s father Yuanqi constantly supplied and gave to the Former Lord, equal to Deran.
translations.idiomatic: Deran’s father, Liu Yuanqi, regularly funded Liu Bei on the same scale as his own son.

sentences.zh: 元起妻曰：「各自一家，何能常爾邪！

translations.literal: Yuanqi’s wife said: “Each is one household—how can it always be thus!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi’s wife protested, “We are not the same household—why should we keep paying his way?”

sentences.zh: 」起曰：「吾宗中有此兒，非常人也。

translations.literal: ” Qi said: “In our clan there is this boy—he is not an ordinary person.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yuanqi answered, “A boy like that in our line is no ordinary child.”

sentences.zh: 」而瓚深與先主相友。

translations.literal: ” And Zan deeply befriended the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gongsun Zan grew especially close to him.

sentences.zh: 瓚年長，先主以兄事之。

translations.literal: Zan was older in years; the Former Lord treated him with elder-brother service.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was the elder, and Liu Bei honored him as an older brother.

sentences.zh: 先主不甚樂讀書，喜狗馬、音樂、美衣服。

translations.literal: The Former Lord was not greatly fond of reading books; he delighted in dogs and horses, music, and fine clothes.
translations.idiomatic: He took little pleasure in books but loved hounds and horses, music, and handsome dress.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺五寸，垂手下膝，顧自見其耳。

translations.literal: His body was seven chi five cun in height; his hanging hands reached below the knees; turning his head he could see his own ears.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi five cun tall, his arms hung past his knees, and he could see his own earlobes when he glanced back.

sentences.zh: 少語言，善下人，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: He spoke little; he was good at placing himself below others; joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke seldom, knew how to defer to others, and kept joy and anger off his face.

sentences.zh: 好交結豪俠，年少爭附之。

translations.literal: He loved to associate and bind heroic knights-errant; youths vied to attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: He sought out bold spirits, and young men crowded to join him.

sentences.zh: 中山大商張世平、蘇雙等貲累千金，販馬周旋於涿郡，見而異之，乃多與之金財。

translations.literal: Great merchants of Zhongshan Zhang Shiping, Su Shuang, and others had wealth piled to a thousand in gold; they traded horses circulating in Zhuo Commandery; seeing him they marveled; then they greatly gave him gold and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongshan horse-dealers Zhang Shiping and Su Shuang, men of fabulous wealth, took one look at him in Zhuo and opened their purses wide.

sentences.zh: 先主由是得用合徒眾。

translations.literal: The Former Lord by this was able to use and assemble followers and a host.
translations.idiomatic: With that silver he began to gather a following.

sentences.zh: 靈帝末，黃巾起，州郡各舉義兵，先主率其屬從校尉鄒靖討黃巾賊有功，除安喜尉。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ling, the Yellow Turbans arose; each commandery and prefecture raised righteous troops; the Former Lord led his followers following Colonel Zou Jing to attack Yellow Turban bandits and had merit; he was appointed captain of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turbans rose at the close of Emperor Ling’s reign, Liu Bei led his men under Colonel Zou Jing, distinguished himself against the rebels, and was named captain of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 〈典略曰：平原劉子平知備有武勇，時張純反叛，青州被詔，遣從事將兵討純，過平原，子平薦備於從事，遂與相隨，遇賊於野，備中創陽死，賊去後，故人以車載之，得免。

translations.literal: 〈The Compendium says: Liu Ziping of Pingyuan knew Bei had martial courage; at that time Zhang Chun rebelled; Qing Province received an edict, sent a clerk leading troops to attack Chun, passed through Pingyuan; Ziping recommended Bei to the clerk; then he followed with him; they met bandits in the wild; Bei was struck wounded and feigned death; after the bandits left, old friends used a cart to carry him; he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Compendium tells how Liu Ziping of Pingyuan, knowing Liu Bei’s valor, recommended him to the provincial clerk marching against Zhang Chun. In a skirmish Liu Bei was wounded and played dead until the raiders left; friends loaded him onto a cart and he survived.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功，為中山安喜尉。〉

translations.literal: Later because of military merit, he became captain of Anxi in Zhongshan.〉
translations.idiomatic: For that service he was later appointed captain of Anxi in Zhongshan.”

sentences.zh: 督郵以公事到縣，先主求謁，不通，直入縛督郵，杖二百，解綬繫其頸着馬枊，

translations.literal: The postal inspector on public business arrived at the county; the Former Lord sought audience; it was not granted; he went straight in, bound the postal inspector, caned two hundred strokes, untied his ribbon and tied it on the inspector’s neck and placed him on the horse hitching-post,
translations.idiomatic: When the postal inspector came on official business and refused him entry, Liu Bei walked straight in, seized the man, gave him two hundred strokes, tied his own official sash around the fellow’s neck, and lashed him to a hitching post,

sentences.zh: 〈五葬反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Wu zang fan [phonetic gloss for 枊].〉
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: the graph is read like wu in the entering tone (a hitching stake).

sentences.zh: 棄官亡命。

translations.literal: He cast away office and fled for his life.
translations.idiomatic: He then abandoned his post and fled.

sentences.zh: 〈典略曰：其後州郡被詔書，其有軍功為長吏者，當沙汰之，備疑在遣中。

translations.literal: 〈The Compendium says: afterward prefectures and commanderies received edicts: those who had military merit and served as senior officials were to be sifted and purged; Bei suspected he was among those to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The Compendium adds that when the court ordered a purge of locally appointed officers with military backgrounds, Liu Bei feared his name was on the list.

sentences.zh: 督郵至縣，當遣備，備素知之。

translations.literal: The postal inspector arrived at the county; he was about to dismiss Bei; Bei had long known it.
translations.idiomatic: When the inspector arrived to dismiss him, Liu Bei had already heard the news.

sentences.zh: 聞督郵在傳舍，備欲求見督郵，督郵稱疾不肯見備，備恨之，因還治，將吏卒更詣傳舍，突入門，言「我被府君密教收督郵」 。

translations.literal: Hearing the postal inspector was in the relay inn, Bei sought to request seeing the postal inspector; the postal inspector claimed illness and was unwilling to see Bei; Bei resented it; therefore he returned to his office, led clerks and soldiers and again went to the relay inn, burst in the gate, saying “I have received the prefect’s secret order to arrest the postal inspector.”
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the man was feigning sickness at the relay inn, Liu Bei went home, gathered his officers, forced the door, and announced that he was acting on secret orders from the prefect to arrest the inspector.

sentences.zh: 遂就床縛之，將出到界，自解其綬以繫督郵頸，縛之著樹，鞭杖百餘下，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Then he went to the bed and bound him; leading him out to the border, he himself untied his ribbon to tie on the postal inspector’s neck, bound him to a tree, whipped and caned more than a hundred strokes, wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He dragged him from his couch, marched him to the county border, looped his own sash around the man’s neck, tied him to a tree, and laid on more than a hundred strokes, meaning to kill him.

sentences.zh: 督郵求哀，乃釋去之。〉

translations.literal: The postal inspector begged pity; then he released and let him go.〉
translations.idiomatic: The inspector’s pleas moved him to spare the man and let him go.”

sentences.zh: 頃之，大將軍何進遣都尉毌丘毅詣丹楊募兵，先主與俱行，至下邳遇賊，力戰有功，除為下密丞。

translations.literal: Before long, General-in-chief He Jin sent Commandant Guanqiu Yi to Danyang to recruit troops; the Former Lord went with him; reaching Xiapi they met bandits; he fought hard and had merit; he was appointed assistant magistrate of Xiami.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward He Jin sent Commandant Guanqiu Yi to Danyang to raise troops; Liu Bei went along, fought bandits hard outside Xiapi, and was named assistant magistrate of Xiami.

sentences.zh: 復去官。

translations.literal: Again he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned that post as well.

sentences.zh: 後為高唐尉，遷為令。

translations.literal: Later he became captain of Gaotang, was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as captain of Gaotang, then as its magistrate.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》云：靈帝末年，備嘗在京師，後與曹公俱還沛國，募召合眾。

translations.literal: 〈The Record of Heroes says: in the last years of Emperor Ling, Bei once was in the capital; later together with Lord Cao he returned to Pei State, recruited and summoned and assembled a host.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes claims that in Emperor Ling’s last years Liu Bei was in the capital, then returned to Pei with Cao Cao to raise men.

sentences.zh: 會靈帝崩，天下大亂，備亦起軍從討董卓。〉

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Ling died; the realm was greatly in chaos; Bei also raised troops and followed in attacking Dong Zhuo.〉
translations.idiomatic: When Ling died and the realm dissolved into chaos, Liu Bei took the field against Dong Zhuo.”

sentences.zh: 為賊所破，往奔中郎將公孫瓚，瓚表為別部司馬，使與青州刺史田楷以拒冀州牧袁紹。

translations.literal: He was broken by bandits; he fled to go to General of the Gentlemen of the Household Gongsun Zan; Zan memorialized him as major of a separate division, sent him with inspector of Qing Province Tian Kai to resist Ji Province Governor Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Routed by raiders, he fled to Gongsun Zan, who memorialized him as major of a separate division and teamed him with Tian Kai, inspector of Qingzhou, against Yuan Shao, governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 數有戰功，試守平原令，後領平原相。

translations.literal: Several times he had battle merit; on trial he guarded as magistrate of Pingyuan; later he concurrently held grand administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated successes he was acting magistrate of Pingyuan, then full grand administrator of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡民劉平素輕先主，恥為之下，使客刺之。

translations.literal: A commandery commoner, Liu Ping, always belittled the Former Lord; he was ashamed to be below him; he sent a retainer to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ping, a local gentleman who despised Liu Bei for ranking above him, sent an assassin.

sentences.zh: 客不忍刺，語之而去。

translations.literal: The retainer could not bear to stab; he told him and left.
translations.idiomatic: The man could not bring himself to strike, confessed the plot, and walked away.

sentences.zh: 其得人心如此。

translations.literal: His winning people’s hearts was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the hold he had on men’s hearts.

sentences.zh: 〈魏書曰：劉平結客刺備，備不知而待客甚厚，客以狀語之而去。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei says: Liu Ping bound retainers to stab Bei; Bei did not know but treated the guest very generously; the guest told him the situation and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei relates that Liu Ping hired a killer who, received with such kindness by Liu Bei, revealed the plot and departed.

sentences.zh: 是時人民饑饉，屯聚鈔暴。

translations.literal: At this time the people were hungry and famished; they gathered in knots and plundered violently.
translations.idiomatic: Famine had driven the people to banditry.

sentences.zh: 備外禦寇難，內豐財施，士之下者，必與同席而坐，同簋而食，無所簡擇。

translations.literal: Bei outwardly defended against bandit hardship; inwardly he enriched wealth and gave; among gentlemen of lower rank, he necessarily sat on the same mat and ate from the same bowl, having no picking or choosing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei beat back raiders abroad and shared his stores at home; the humblest soldier sat at his mat and ate from his bowl without distinction.

sentences.zh: 眾多歸焉。〉

translations.literal: The multitude greatly attached to him.〉
translations.idiomatic: Men flocked to him in numbers.”

sentences.zh: 先主還小沛，

translations.literal: The Former Lord returned to Little Pei,
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord withdrew to Little Pei,

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：備軍在廣陵，飢餓困踧，吏士大小自相噉食，窮餓侵逼，欲還小沛，遂使吏請降布。

translations.literal: 〈The Record of Heroes says: Bei’s army was at Guangling, hungry and pressed in distress; clerks and soldiers great and small mutually ate one another; extreme hunger pressed close; wishing to return to Little Pei, then he sent clerks to request surrender to Bu.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes tells how, starving at Guangling until his men fed on one another, Liu Bei begged Lu Bu for shelter and a road back to Little Pei.

sentences.zh: 布令備還州，并勢擊術。

translations.literal: Bu ordered Bei to return to the province, combine forces, and strike Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bu sent him back to Xu province to join forces against Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 具刺史車馬僮僕，發遣備妻子部曲家屬於泗水上，祖道相樂。

translations.literal: He fully provided inspector chariots, horses, servants; he dispatched Bei’s wife, children, retainers, and family dependents on the Si River’s bank; they feasted the road-gods and mutually rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bu furnished an inspector’s equipage and sent Liu Bei’s wives, children, and troops across the Si with a farewell feast.

sentences.zh: 魏書曰：諸將謂布曰：「備數反覆難養，宜早圖之。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei says: the various generals said to Bu: “Bei repeatedly turns and is hard to nurture; you should early plot him.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei records Lu Bu’s officers warning him, “Liu Bei is a proven turncoat—deal with him now.”

sentences.zh: 」布不聽，以狀語備。

translations.literal: ” Bu did not listen; he told Bei the situation.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lu Bu refused and repeated the warning to Liu Bei himself.

sentences.zh: 備心不安而求自託，使人說布，求屯小沛，布乃遣之。〉

translations.literal: Bei’s heart was uneasy and he sought to entrust himself; he sent men to persuade Bu, requesting to garrison Little Pei; Bu then sent him.〉
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Liu Bei begged leave to garrison Little Pei; Lu Bu consented.”

sentences.zh: 復合兵得萬餘人。

translations.literal: Again he combined troops and obtained more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: There he rebuilt an army of over ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 呂布惡之，自出兵攻先主，先主敗走歸曹公。

translations.literal: Lu Bu hated it; he himself led troops to attack the Former Lord; the Former Lord was defeated and fled to return to Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bu turned on him, drove him from the field, and Liu Bei fled to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 曹公厚遇之，以為豫州牧。

translations.literal: Lord Cao treated him generously; made him governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao received him handsomely and named him governor of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 將至沛收散卒，給其軍糧，益與兵使東擊布。

translations.literal: He was about to reach Pei to collect scattered troops, supply his army grain, increase and give him troops, sending him east to attack Bu.
translations.idiomatic: He was to proceed to Pei to rally stragglers, draw rations, receive reinforcements, and march east against Lu Bu.

sentences.zh: 布遣高順攻之，曹公遣夏侯惇往，不能救，為順所敗，復虜先主妻子送布。

translations.literal: Bu sent Gao Shun to attack him; Lord Cao sent Xiahou Dun to go; he could not save; was defeated by Shun; again captured the Former Lord’s wife and children and sent them to Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bu sent Gao Shun against him; Cao Cao’s relief column under Xiahou Dun failed, and Liu Bei’s family was captured again and sent to Lu Bu’s camp.

sentences.zh: 曹公自出東征，

translations.literal: Lord Cao himself went out on an eastern campaign,
translations.idiomatic: Then Cao Cao took the field in person on an eastern campaign,

sentences.zh: 〈英雄記曰：建安三年春，布使人齎金欲詣河內買馬，為備兵所鈔。

translations.literal: 〈The Record of Heroes says: in the spring of the third year of Jian’an, Bu sent men carrying gold wishing to go to Henei to buy horses; they were plundered by Bei’s troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes notes that in the spring of Jian’an 3 Lu Bu’s agents carrying gold to buy horses in Henei were robbed by Liu Bei’s men.

sentences.zh: 布由是遣中郎將高順、北地太守張遼等攻備。

translations.literal: Bu for this reason sent General of the Gentlemen of the Household Gao Shun, grand administrator of Beidi Zhang Liao, and others to attack Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bu thereupon dispatched Gao Shun and Zhang Liao, grand administrator of Beidi, against Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 九月，遂破沛城，備單身走，獲其妻息。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, then they broke Pei city; Bei alone fled on foot; they captured his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they stormed Pei; Liu Bei escaped alone while his family was taken.

sentences.zh: 十月，曹公自征布，備於梁國界中與曹公相遇，遂隨公俱東征。〉

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Lord Cao himself campaigned against Bu; Bei within the borders of Liang State met Lord Cao; then he followed the lord together on the eastern campaign.〉
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Cao Cao marched on Lu Bu; Liu Bei joined him in Liang and accompanied the eastern expedition.”

sentences.zh: 助先主圍布於下邳，生禽布。

translations.literal: Lord Cao aided the Former Lord in besieging Bu at Xiapi; alive they seized Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao joined him in the siege of Lu Bu at Xiapi and took Lu Bu alive.

sentences.zh: 先主復得妻子，從曹公還許。

translations.literal: The Former Lord again obtained wife and children; following Lord Cao he returned to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei recovered his family and followed Cao Cao back to the capital at Xu.

sentences.zh: 表先主為左將軍，禮之愈重，出則同輿，坐則同席。

translations.literal: He memorialized the Former Lord as General of the Left; his courtesies to him grew heavier; going out then same carriage, sitting then same mat.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had him named general of the left and honored him so highly that they rode in the same carriage and sat on the same mat.

sentences.zh: 袁術欲經徐州北就袁紹，曹公遣先主督朱靈、路招要擊術。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu wished to pass through Xu Province northward to join Yuan Shao; Lord Cao sent the Former Lord to supervise Zhu Ling and Lu Zhao to intercept and strike Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shu tried to cross Xu province north to Yuan Shao, Cao Cao sent Liu Bei with Zhu Ling and Lu Zhao to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 未至，術病死。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Shu died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu died of sickness before they could engage.

sentences.zh: 先主未出時，獻帝舅車騎將軍董承

translations.literal: Before the Former Lord had gone out, Emperor Xian’s uncle-by-marriage General of Chariots and Cavalry Dong Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Before Liu Bei marched, Emperor Xian’s uncle by marriage, General of chariots and cavalry Dong Cheng,

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：董承，漢靈帝母董太后之侄，於獻帝為丈人。

translations.literal: 〈Your subject Songzhi’s note: Dong Cheng was nephew of Empress Dowager Dong, mother of Han Emperor Ling; toward Emperor Xian he was father-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Dong Cheng was a nephew of Empress Dowager Dong and, by Han usage, counted as the emperor’s father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 蓋古無丈人之名，故謂之舅也。〉

translations.literal: Probably antiquity had no name “father-in-law”; therefore he was called uncle.〉
translations.idiomatic: The text calls him “uncle” because classical usage lacked the later term for a wife’s father.”

sentences.zh: 辭受帝衣帶中密詔，當誅曹公。

translations.literal: In words he received the emperor’s secret edict in the belt of the robe, ordering to execute Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: had received a secret edict sewn in the emperor’s sash, charging him to kill Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 先主未發。

translations.literal: The Former Lord had not yet set out.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei had not yet moved.

sentences.zh: 是時曹公從容謂先主曰：「今天下英雄，唯使君與操耳。

translations.literal: At this time Lord Cao leisurely said to the Former Lord: “Now the realm’s heroes are only your excellency and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said to him over wine, “The only heroes left under heaven are you and I.”

sentences.zh: 本初之徒，不足數也。

translations.literal: Benchu’s sort are not worth counting.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yuan Shao are not worth naming.”

sentences.zh: 」先主方食，失匕箸。

translations.literal: ” The Former Lord was just eating; he dropped spoon and chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Bei, caught mid-meal, dropped his chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》云：于時正當雷震，備因謂操曰：「聖人云‘迅雷風烈必變’，良有以也。

translations.literal: 〈The Treatise on Huayang says: at that time it happened there was thunderclap; Bei therefore said to Cao: “The sage said ‘sudden thunder and fierce wind surely change’—truly there is reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Huayang adds that a peal of thunder gave Liu Bei cover to mutter to Cao Cao about the sage’s words on sudden thunder and violent wind.

sentences.zh: 一震之威，乃可至於此也！」〉

translations.literal: The awe of one thunderclap—then can reach to this!”〉
translations.idiomatic: “A single clap,” he said, “can shake a man so!””

sentences.zh: 遂與承及長水校尉种輯、將軍吳子蘭、王子服等同謀。

translations.literal: Then together with Cheng and Colonel of the Chang Waters Zhong Ji, generals Wu Zilan, Wang Zifu, and others he plotted alike.
translations.idiomatic: He then conspired with Dong Cheng, Colonel Zhong Ji of the Chang River regiment, and the generals Wu Zilan and Wang Zifu.

sentences.zh: 會見使，未發。

translations.literal: It happened he received a mission; had not yet set out.
translations.idiomatic: Just then he received another court assignment and did not move against Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 事覺，承等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: The affair was discovered; Cheng and the rest all submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked, Dong Cheng and his confederates were put to death.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：承等與備謀未發，而備出。

translations.literal: 〈The Daily Notes of Emperor Xian says: Cheng and others with Bei plotted not yet set out, but Bei went out.
translations.idiomatic: The Daily Notes of Emperor Xian record that Dong Cheng and Liu Bei had not yet acted when Liu Bei was sent away.

sentences.zh: 承謂服曰：「郭多有數百兵，壞李傕數万人，但足下與我同不耳！

translations.literal: Cheng said to Fu: “Guo Si had several hundred troops, ruined Li Jue’s several tens of thousands of men—only you and I are the same or not!
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng told Wang Zifu, “Guo Si once broke Li Jue’s host of tens of thousands with a few hundred men—will you stand with me or not?”

sentences.zh: 昔呂不韋之門，須子楚而後高，今吾與子由是也。

translations.literal: Formerly at Lu Buwei’s gate, it waited for Zichu afterward then was high; now I and you are by this.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Buwei’s house rose only when Zichu appeared; you and I are in the same case.”

sentences.zh: 」服曰：「惶懼不敢當，且兵又少。

translations.literal: ” Fu said: “Fearful and trembling I dare not bear it; moreover troops are also few.
translations.idiomatic: ” Wang answered, “I am too afraid, and our soldiers are too few.”

sentences.zh: 」承曰：「舉事訖，得曹公成兵，顧不足邪？

translations.literal: ” Cheng said: “When the deed is finished, obtaining Lord Cao’s completed troops—is it not enough?
translations.idiomatic: ” Dong Cheng replied, “Once we move, we seize Cao Cao’s trained troops—will that not suffice?”

sentences.zh: 」服曰：「今京師豈有所任乎？

translations.literal: ” Fu said: “Now in the capital is there indeed someone appointed?
translations.idiomatic: ” “Who in the capital,” Wang asked, “can we rely on?”

sentences.zh: 」承曰：「長水校尉种輯、議郎吳碩是我腹心辦事者。

translations.literal: ” Cheng said: “Colonel of the Chang Waters Zhong Ji, gentleman-adviser Wu Shuo are my inner-belly heart men who manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: ” “Colonel Zhong Ji of the Chang River regiment and Gentleman-adviser Wu Shuo are my trusted agents.”

sentences.zh: 」遂定計。〉

translations.literal: ” Then they fixed the plan.〉
translations.idiomatic: ” With that the plot was set.”

sentences.zh: 先主據下邳。

translations.literal: The Former Lord occupied Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord seized Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 靈等還，先主乃殺徐州刺史車冑，留關羽守下邳，而身還小沛。

translations.literal: When Ling and the others returned, the Former Lord then killed Xu Province Inspector Che Zhou, left Guan Yu guarding Xiapi, while he himself returned to Little Pei.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ling’s column came back, Liu Bei killed the inspector of Xu province, Che Zhou, left Guan Yu at Xiapi, and withdrew to Little Pei.

sentences.zh: 〈胡沖《吳歷》曰：曹公數遣親近密覘諸將有賓客酒食者，輒因事害之。

translations.literal: 〈Hu Chong’s Record of Wu says: Lord Cao repeatedly sent intimates secretly to spy on generals who had guests for wine and food; then on pretext harmed them.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chong’s Record of Wu says Cao Cao often sent agents to spy on generals who entertained, then found excuses to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 備時閉門，將人種蕪菁，曹公使人闚門。

translations.literal: Bei at that time closed the gate, led men planting turnips; Lord Cao sent men to peep at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei shut his gates and set his men to planting turnips while Cao Cao’s spies watched.

sentences.zh: 既去，備謂張飛、關羽曰：「吾豈種菜者乎？

translations.literal: After they left, Bei said to Zhang Fei and Guan Yu: “Am I indeed a vegetable planter?
translations.idiomatic: When they left, he said to Zhang Fei and Guan Yu, “Do I look like a gardener?”

sentences.zh: 曹公必有疑意，不可復留。

translations.literal: Lord Cao surely has suspicious intent; we cannot again remain.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao already doubts us—we cannot stay.”

sentences.zh: 」其夜開後柵，與飛等輕騎俱去，所得賜遺衣服，悉封留之，乃往小沛收合兵眾。

translations.literal: ” That night he opened the rear palisade; with Fei and others on light horses all departed; obtained gifts and bestowed clothes, all sealed and left them; then went to Little Pei to gather and combine troops and hosts.
translations.idiomatic: ” That night he slipped out the rear stockade with Zhang Fei and a light escort, sealed up every gift robe Cao had given him, and rode to Little Pei to rally his army.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：魏武帝遣先主統諸將要擊袁術，郭嘉等並諫，魏武不從，其事顯然，非因種菜遁逃而去。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi’s note: Emperor Wu of Wei dispatched the Former Lord to command the various generals to intercept and strike Yuan Shu; Guo Jia and others together remonstrated; Emperor Wu did not follow; the affair is clearly thus—not because of planting vegetables he fled and escaped and left.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi observes that Wei Emperor Wu sent Liu Bei against Yuan Shu over Guo Jia’s objections—a public mission—so the turnip story cannot explain his flight.

sentences.zh: 如胡沖所云，何乖僻之甚乎！〉

translations.literal: As Hu Chong said—how perverse in the extreme!〉
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chong’s tale is far too odd to credit.”

sentences.zh: 東海昌霸反，郡縣多叛曹公為先主，眾數萬人，遣孫乾與袁紹連和，曹公遣劉岱、王忠擊之，不克。

translations.literal: In Donghai Chang Ba rebelled; commanderies and counties for the most part revolted from Lord Cao for the Former Lord; the host was several tens of thousands of men; he sent Sun Qian to ally with Yuan Shao; Lord Cao sent Liu Dai and Wang Zhong to strike them; they did not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Ba of Donghai rose, many counties threw off Cao Cao for Liu Bei, swelling his ranks past ten thousand. Sun Qian went to treat with Yuan Shao while Cao Cao sent Liu Dai and Wang Zhong against them without success.

sentences.zh: 五年，曹公東征先主，先主敗績。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Lord Cao campaigned east against the Former Lord; the Former Lord was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jian'an Cao Cao marched east and crushed him.

sentences.zh: 〈魏書曰：是時，公方有急於官渡，乃分留諸將屯官渡，自勒精兵征備。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei says: at this time the lord was pressed at Guandu; then he divided and left the various generals to garrison Guandu; himself led crack troops to campaign against Bei.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei explains that Cao Cao, hard pressed at Guandu, left part of his army there and led picked troops east against Liu Bei himself.

sentences.zh: 備初謂公與大敵連，不得東，而候騎卒至，言曹公自來。

translations.literal: Bei at first thought the lord was tied to a great foe and could not come east; but patrol riders suddenly arrived, saying Lord Cao himself was coming.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei had assumed Cao Cao was pinned by a major enemy and could not leave the west—until scouts galloped in with word that Cao Cao was coming in person.

sentences.zh: 備大驚，然猶未信。

translations.literal: Bei was greatly startled, yet still did not believe.
translations.idiomatic: He was stunned but still half doubted the report.

sentences.zh: 自將數十騎出望公軍，見麾旌，便棄眾而走。〉

translations.literal: Himself leading several tens of riders he went out to gaze on the lord’s army; seeing banners and standards, then he cast away the host and fled.〉
translations.idiomatic: He rode out with a few dozen horsemen to look for himself; when he saw Cao Cao’s banners he abandoned his army and fled.”

sentences.zh: 曹公盡收其眾，虜先主妻子，並禽關羽以歸。

translations.literal: Lord Cao wholly gathered his host; captured the Former Lord’s wife and children; and together seized Guan Yu to return.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao scooped up his force, took his wives and children, and captured Guan Yu as well.

sentences.zh: 先主走青州。

translations.literal: The Former Lord fled to Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord fled into Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史袁譚，先主故茂才也，將步騎迎先主。

translations.literal: Inspector of Qing Province Yuan Tan was the Former Lord’s former recommended flourishing talent; he led infantry and cavalry to welcome the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan, inspector of Qingzhou, who had once recommended Liu Bei as a flourishing talent, came out with foot and horse to meet him.

sentences.zh: 先主隨譚到平原，譚馳使白紹。

translations.literal: The Former Lord followed Tan to Pingyuan; Tan galloped a messenger to report to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei accompanied him to Pingyuan while Yuan Tan sent a fast courier to Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 紹遣將道路奉迎，身去鄴二百里，與先主相見。

translations.literal: Shao sent a general on the road to receive him; his person left Ye two hundred li and met the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao dispatched an escort and rode two hundred li south from Ye to welcome him in person.

sentences.zh: 〈魏書曰：備歸紹，紹父子傾心敬重。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei says: when Bei returned to Shao, Shao father and son poured out their hearts in respect.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei notes that father and son Yuan received him with full courtesy and esteem.”

sentences.zh: 駐月餘日，所失亡士卒稍稍來集。

translations.literal: He halted more than a month; lost and scattered soldiers gradually came to gather.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed over a month while scattered troops trickled back.

sentences.zh: 曹公與袁紹相拒於官渡，汝南黃巾劉辟等叛曹公應紹。

translations.literal: Lord Cao and Yuan Shao faced each other at Guandu; Runan Yellow Turbans Liu Pi and others rebelled from Lord Cao and responded to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao and Yuan Shao faced off at Guandu, the Runan Yellow Turbans under Liu Pi rose against Cao in Yuan Shao's name.

sentences.zh: 紹遣先主將兵與辟等略許下。

translations.literal: Shao sent the Former Lord to lead troops with Pi and others to raid the area below Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent Liu Bei with Liu Pi to raid the country south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 關羽亡歸先主。

translations.literal: Guan Yu fled and returned to the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu broke free and rejoined him.

sentences.zh: 曹公遣曹仁將兵擊先主，先主還紹軍，陰欲離紹，乃說紹南連荊州牧劉表。

translations.literal: Lord Cao sent Cao Ren to lead troops to strike the Former Lord; the Former Lord returned to Shao’s army; secretly wishing to leave Shao, then he persuaded Shao southward to ally with Jing Province Governor Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Cao Ren against him; Liu Bei pulled back to Yuan Shao's camp but already meant to slip away, and talked Yuan Shao into linking south with Governor Liu Biao of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹遣先主將本兵復至汝南，與賊龔都等合，眾數千人。

translations.literal: Shao sent the Former Lord to lead his original troops again to Runan; he combined with bandit Gong Du and others; the host was several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao then sent him back to Runan with his own command to join Gong Du's band, a force of a few thousand.

sentences.zh: 曹公遣蔡陽擊之，為先主所殺。

translations.literal: Lord Cao sent Cai Yang to strike him; he was killed by the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao dispatched Cai Yang, whom Liu Bei cut down.

sentences.zh: 曹公既破紹，自南擊先主。

translations.literal: After Lord Cao had broken Shao, himself south he struck the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Yuan Shao, Cao Cao turned south against Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 先主遣麋竺、孫乾與劉表相聞，表自郊迎，以上賓禮待之，益其兵，使屯新野。

translations.literal: The Former Lord sent Mi Zhu and Sun Qian to communicate with Liu Biao; Biao himself went to the suburbs to welcome; treated him with upper-guest ritual; increased his troops; made him garrison Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sent Mi Zhu and Sun Qian ahead; Liu Biao met him beyond the walls as an honored guest, enlarged his command, and posted him at Xinye.

sentences.zh: 荊州豪傑歸先主者日益多，表疑其心，陰禦之。

translations.literal: Jingzhou heroes who attached to the Former Lord daily grew more numerous; Biao suspected his heart; secretly guarded against him.
translations.idiomatic: As more Jingzhou notables rallied to Liu Bei, Liu Biao grew wary and quietly checked him.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：備住荊州數年，嘗於表坐起至廁，見髀裡肉生，慨然流涕。

translations.literal: 〈The Springs and Autumns of the Nine Provinces says: Bei dwelt in Jingzhou several years; once rising from sitting with Biao he went to the privy; seeing flesh on his thighs had grown, he sighed and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: The Springs and Autumns of the Nine Provinces tells how, after years at Liu Biao's court, Liu Bei rose from the mat to relieve himself, noticed flesh thickening on his thighs, and wept.

sentences.zh: 還坐，表怪問備，備曰：「吾常身不離鞍，髀肉皆消。

translations.literal: Returning to sit, Biao wondered and asked Bei; Bei said: “I constantly never left the saddle; flesh on the thighs all vanished.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Biao asked why, he said, “In the old days I never left the saddle; the flesh here wasted away.”

sentences.zh: 今不復騎，髀裏肉生。

translations.literal: Now I no longer ride; flesh inside the thighs has grown.
translations.idiomatic: “Now I seldom ride, and it grows again.”

sentences.zh: 日月若馳，老將至矣，而功業不建，是以悲耳。

translations.literal: Sun and moon like galloping; old age will arrive; yet merit and enterprise are not established—therefore I grieve.”
translations.idiomatic: “The years fly; old age comes, yet I have built nothing—hence my sorrow.”

sentences.zh: 」《世語》曰：備屯樊城，劉表禮焉，憚其為人，不甚信用。

translations.literal: ” The Shiyu says: Bei was garrisoned at Fancheng; Liu Biao treated him with ritual, feared his person, did not greatly trust and employ.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Shiyu adds that though Liu Biao treated him well at Fancheng, he feared his character and seldom gave him real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 曾請備宴會，蒯越、蔡瑁欲因會取備，備覺之，偽如廁，潛遁出。

translations.literal: Once he invited Bei to a banquet; Kuai Yue and Cai Mao wished by the banquet to seize Bei; Bei perceived it; feigned going to the privy; secretly slipped out and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet Kuai Yue and Cai Mao meant to seize him; he sensed the trap, excused himself to the privy, and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 所乘馬名的盧，騎的盧走，墮襄陽城西檀溪水中，溺不得出。

translations.literal: The horse he rode was named Dilu; riding Dilu he ran, fell into Tan Stream’s waters west of Xiangyang city, sank and could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: His horse Dilu carried him into the Tan Brook west of Xiangyang, where it floundered and could not climb the bank.

sentences.zh: 備急曰：「的盧：今日厄矣，可努力！

translations.literal: Bei urgently said: “Dilu: today is peril; you can strive!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei cried, “Dilu, this is our doom—give me everything you have!”

sentences.zh: 」的盧乃一踴三丈，遂得過，乘桴渡河，中流而追者至，以表意謝之，曰：「何去之速乎！

translations.literal: ” Dilu then in one leap three zhang; then was able to cross; riding a raft crossed the river; midstream pursuers arrived; with Biao’s intent he thanked them, saying: “Why leave so fast!
translations.idiomatic: ” The horse leaped three zhang in one bound and gained the far bank. He rafted a river, and as pursuers closed midstream he excused himself in Liu Biao's name: “Why such haste to go?”

sentences.zh: 」孫盛曰：此不然之言。

translations.literal: ” Sun Sheng says: this is not so speech.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Sheng dismisses the tale as untrue.

sentences.zh: 備時羈旅，客主勢殊，若有此變，豈敢晏然終表之世而無釁故乎？

translations.literal: Bei at that time was a wandering guest; guest and host power was different; if there were this change, how dare he peacefully finish Biao’s age without incident cause?
translations.idiomatic: A dependent guest in such peril could not have stayed at ease through Liu Biao's reign without open rupture.

sentences.zh: 此皆世俗妄說，非事實也。〉

translations.literal: These are all vulgar world reckless sayings, not factual matters.〉
translations.idiomatic: It is mere gossip, not fact.”

sentences.zh: 使拒夏侯惇、于禁等於博望。

translations.literal: He was sent to resist Xiahou Dun, Yu Jin, and others at Bowang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao sent him to hold Xiahou Dun and Yu Jin at Bowang.

sentences.zh: 久之，先主設伏兵，一旦自燒屯偽遁，惇等追之，為伏兵所破。

translations.literal: After a long time, the Former Lord set ambush troops; in one morning himself burned the camp feigning flight; Dun and others pursued them; were broken by ambush troops.
translations.idiomatic: After long stalemate Liu Bei fired his camp and feigned retreat; Xiahou Dun pursued into an ambush and was routed.

sentences.zh: 十二年，曹公北征烏丸，先主說表襲許，表不能用。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Lord Cao north campaigned the Wuhuan; the Former Lord persuaded Biao to raid Xu; Biao could not use it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Jian'an, while Cao Cao marched north against the Wuhuan, Liu Bei urged Liu Biao to strike the capital at Xu; Liu Biao would not act.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：曹公自柳城還，表謂備曰：「不用君言，故為失此大會。

translations.literal: 〈The Springs and Autumns of Han and Jin says: when Lord Cao returned from Liucheng, Biao said to Bei: “Not using your lord’s words, therefore missed this great opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: The Springs and Autumns of Han and Jin records that when Cao Cao returned from Liucheng, Liu Biao told him, “I ignored your counsel and missed the chance.”

sentences.zh: 」備曰：「今天下分裂，日尋干戈，事會之來，豈有終極乎？

translations.literal: ” Bei said: “Now the realm is split apart; day by day they seek shields and spears; when occasions come, how can there be an ultimate end?
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Bei answered, “The empire is torn; arms clash every day. Openings come and go—who can say when the last will be?”

sentences.zh: 若能應之於後者，則此未足為恨也。」〉

translations.literal: If one can respond to them afterward, then this is not enough to be regret.”〉
translations.idiomatic: “Seize the next one, and this need not rank as regret.””

sentences.zh: 曹公南征表，會表卒，

translations.literal: Lord Cao south campaigned Biao; it happened Biao died,
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched south against Liu Biao just as Liu Biao died,

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：表病，上備領荊州刺史。

translations.literal: 〈The Record of Heroes says: Biao was ill; he memorialized upward that Bei concurrently hold inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes states that a dying Liu Biao memorialized Liu Bei as acting inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏書曰：表病篤，託國於備，顧謂曰：「我兒不才，而諸將並零落，我死之後，卿便攝荊州。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei says: Biao was critically ill; he entrusted the state to Bei; turning he said: “My sons lack talent, yet the various generals are all scattered; after I die, you shall take Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei claims that on his deathbed Liu Biao entrusted the province to Liu Bei, saying, “My sons are worthless and my generals are spent; after my death you must take charge of Jingzhou.”

sentences.zh: 」備曰：「諸子自賢，君其憂病。

translations.literal: ” Bei said: “The sons are themselves worthy; you worry about illness.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Bei replied, “Your sons are able men; worry only about your health.”

sentences.zh: 」或勸備宜從表言，備曰：「此人待我厚，今從其言，人必以我為薄，所不忍也。

translations.literal: ” Someone urged Bei ought to follow Biao’s words; Bei said: “This person treated me generously; now if I follow his words, people will surely think me cold—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: ” When others urged him to accept, he said, “He has been generous; if I seized his charge now, the world would call me faithless, and I could not bear that.”

sentences.zh: 」臣松之以為表夫妻素愛琮，捨適立庶，情計久定，無緣臨終舉荊州以授備，此亦不然之言。〉

translations.literal: ” Your subject Songzhi considers that Biao husband and wife always loved Cong; discarding the heir and establishing the younger son—their feelings and plans were long fixed; there was no reason at the deathbed to raise Jing Province and hand it to Bei—this too is not so speech.〉
translations.idiomatic: ” Pei Songzhi objects that Liu Biao and his wife had long meant to set younger Liu Cong on the throne, so a deathbed cession to Liu Bei is implausible.”

sentences.zh: 子琮代立，遣使請降。

translations.literal: Son Cong replaced him and stood; sent envoys requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong succeeded him and sent envoys to surrender to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 先主屯樊，不知曹公卒至，至宛乃聞之，遂將其眾去。

translations.literal: The Former Lord was garrisoned at Fan; he did not know Lord Cao suddenly arrived; reaching Wan then he heard it; then he led his host away.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was at Fan and did not learn that Cao Cao had struck until word reached him at Wan; he then marched his people south.

sentences.zh: 過襄陽，諸葛亮說先主攻琮，荊州可有。

translations.literal: Passing Xiangyang, Zhuge Liang persuaded the Former Lord to attack Cong; Jing Province could be had.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang Zhuge Liang urged him to strike Liu Cong and take the province.

sentences.zh: 先主曰：「吾不忍也。」

translations.literal: The Former Lord said: “I cannot bear it.”
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord said, “I cannot bring myself to do it.”

sentences.zh: 〈孔衍《漢魏春秋》曰：劉琮乞降，不敢告備。

translations.literal: 〈Kong Yan’s Springs and Autumns of Han and Wei says: Liu Cong begged surrender; he did not dare tell Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yan’s Springs and Autumns of Han and Wei says Liu Cong surrendered in secret without informing Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 備亦不知，久之乃覺，遣所親問琮。

translations.literal: Bei also did not know; after a long time then he perceived; he sent those close to ask Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei knew nothing until long afterward; he sent confidants to question Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 琮令宋忠詣備宣旨。

translations.literal: Cong ordered Song Zhong to go to Bei and proclaim the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong sent Song Zhong to deliver the news.

sentences.zh: 是時曹公在宛，備乃大驚駭，謂忠曰：「卿諸人作事如此，不早相語，今禍至方告我，不亦太劇乎！

translations.literal: At this time Lord Cao was at Wan; Bei then was greatly shocked; he said to Zhong: “You gentlemen conduct affairs thus—not early telling each other; now disaster has arrived only then you tell me—is it not too severe!
translations.idiomatic: By then Cao Cao was already at Wan. Liu Bei rounded on Song Zhong: “Why keep me in the dark until disaster is on us?”

sentences.zh: 」引刀向忠曰：「今斷卿頭，不足以解忿，亦恥大丈夫臨別復殺卿輩！

translations.literal: ” He drew a knife toward Zhong and said: “Now cutting off your head is not enough to dissolve rage; it is also shame for a great man at parting again to kill you lot!
translations.idiomatic: ” He drew his blade on Song Zhong: “Beheading you would not ease my wrath, and a man of honor does not butcher envoys at a parting.”

sentences.zh: 」遣忠去，乃呼部曲議。

translations.literal: ” He sent Zhong away; then he called retainers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: ” He dismissed Song Zhong and called his officers in council.

sentences.zh: 或勸備劫將琮及荊州吏士徑南到江陵，備答曰：「劉荊州臨亡託我以孤遺，背信自濟，吾所不為，死何面目以見劉荊州乎！」〉

translations.literal: Someone urged Bei to seize and lead Cong and Jingzhou clerks and soldiers straight south to Jiangling; Bei answered: “Liu Jingzhou at death entrusted me with the orphaned remnant; betraying trust to save myself—what I will not do—dead, what face to see Liu Jingzhou!”〉
translations.idiomatic: When urged to seize Liu Cong and bolt for Jiangling, he answered, “Liu Biao trusted his orphan to me; I will not save myself by treachery, nor face him in death.””

sentences.zh: 乃駐馬呼琮，琮懼不能起。

translations.literal: Then he reined his horse and called Cong; Cong feared and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He reined in and hailed Liu Cong, who was too terrified to rise.

sentences.zh: 琮左右及荊州人多歸先主。

translations.literal: Cong’s attendants and Jingzhou people for the most part attached to the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong’s household and many Jingzhou men went over to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 〈典略曰：備過辭表墓，遂涕泣而去。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Compendium says: Bei passed to bid farewell at Biao’s tomb; then weeping he departed.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Compendium adds that he wept at Liu Biao’s grave before leaving.”

sentences.zh: 比到當陽，眾十餘萬，輜重數千兩，日行十餘里，別遣關羽乘船數百艘，使會江陵。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Dangyang, the host was more than a hundred thousand; baggage trains several thousand vehicles; they marched not more than ten-plus li a day; separately he sent Guan Yu embarking on several hundred boats, ordering to meet at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: By Dangyang his following passed a hundred thousand; baggage wagons numbered in the thousands, yet they crept barely ten li a day while Guan Yu took several hundred boats toward a rendezvous at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 或謂先主曰：「宜速行保江陵，今雖擁大眾，被甲者少，若曹公兵至，何以拒之？

translations.literal: Someone said to the Former Lord: “You ought to speed march and protect Jiangling; now although you hold a great host, armored men are few; if Lord Cao’s troops arrive, how will you resist?
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him, “Race for Jiangling; this throng is mostly unarmored—how will you stand against Cao Cao?”

sentences.zh: 」先主曰：「夫濟大事必以人為本，今人歸吾，吾何忍棄去！」

translations.literal: ” The Former Lord said: “To accomplish a great matter must take people as root; now people attach to me—how can I bear to cast them away!”
translations.idiomatic: ” He answered, “Great deeds rest on men; these people trust me—I will not abandon them.”

sentences.zh: 〈習鑿齒曰：先主雖顛沛險難而信義愈明，勢偪事危而言不失道。

translations.literal: 〈Xi Zuochi says: although the Former Lord was tossed in peril and hardship, faith and righteousness grew clearer; power pressed, affairs perilous, yet speech did not lose the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi praises him: even in extremity his good faith shone brighter, and his words stayed true to the right path.

sentences.zh: 追景升之顧，則情感三軍；

translations.literal: Pursuing Jingsheng’s regard, then emotion moved the three armies;
translations.idiomatic: His debt to Liu Biao moved the whole army;

sentences.zh: 戀赴義之士，則甘與同敗。

translations.literal: loving knights who rushed to righteousness, then willingly shared the same defeat.
translations.idiomatic: his care for men who had chosen honor made him willing to share their ruin.

sentences.zh: 觀其所以結物情者，豈徒投醪撫寒含蓼問疾而已哉！

translations.literal: Observe how he bound the feelings of things—was it only casting ale, stroking cold, holding wormwood, asking illness!
translations.idiomatic: See how he won hearts: not merely by sharing wine and tending the sick!

sentences.zh: 其終濟大業，不亦宜乎！〉

translations.literal: That he in the end accomplished the great enterprise—is it not fitting!〉
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder he finished the great work.”

sentences.zh: 曹公以江陵有軍實，恐先主據之，乃釋輜重，輕軍到襄陽。

translations.literal: Lord Cao because Jiangling had military stores, feared the Former Lord would occupy it; then he cast off baggage trains, light army reached Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Liu Bei would seize Jiangling and its arsenals, Cao Cao shed his baggage train and raced a light column to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 聞先主已過，曹公將精騎五千急追之，一日一夜行三百餘里，及於當陽之長坂。

translations.literal: Hearing the Former Lord had already passed, Lord Cao led crack cavalry five thousand urgently pursued him; one day one night they marched more than three hundred li; overtook at Dangyang’s Chang Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Liu Bei had already passed, he took five thousand picked horsemen and rode day and night over three hundred li to overtake him at Changban south of Dangyang.

sentences.zh: 先主棄妻子，與諸葛亮、張飛、趙雲等數十騎走，曹公大獲其人眾輜重。

translations.literal: The Former Lord cast away wife and children; with Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun, and others several tens of riders fled; Lord Cao greatly captured his people, host, and baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei abandoned his family and fled with Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun, and a few dozen horsemen while Cao Cao seized his masses and baggage.

sentences.zh: 先主斜趨漢津，適與羽船會，得濟沔，遇表長子江夏太守琦眾萬餘人，與俱到夏口。

translations.literal: The Former Lord slanted toward Han Ford; happened to meet Yu’s boats; was able to cross Mian; met Biao’s eldest son Jiangxia grand administrator Qi’s host more than ten thousand men; together arrived at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: He angled for the Han ford, met Guan Yu’s flotilla, crossed the Mian, and joined Liu Qi, Liu Biao’s eldest son and grand administrator of Jiangxia, with ten thousand men; together they reached Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 先主遣諸葛亮自結於孫權，

translations.literal: The Former Lord sent Zhuge Liang himself to bind with Sun Quan,
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhuge Liang to treat with Sun Quan,

sentences.zh: 〈江表傳曰：孫權遣魯肅弔劉表二子，并令與備相結。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions from Beyond the River says: Sun Quan sent Lu Su to condole Liu Biao’s two sons, and ordered him also to bind with Bei.
translations.idiomatic: The Traditions from Beyond the River states that Sun Quan sent Lu Su to console Liu Biao’s sons and to open talks with Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 肅未至而曹公已濟漢津。

translations.literal: Su had not yet arrived but Lord Cao had already crossed Han Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Before Lu Su arrived, Cao Cao had already crossed the Han ford.

sentences.zh: 肅故進前，與備相遇於當陽。

translations.literal: Su therefore advanced forward; met Bei at Dangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su pressed on and met Liu Bei at Dangyang.

sentences.zh: 因宣權旨，論天下事勢，致殷勤之意。

translations.literal: Thereupon he proclaimed Quan’s intent, discussed the realm’s situation of affairs, conveyed earnest cordiality.
translations.idiomatic: He delivered Sun Quan’s message, reviewed the strategic picture, and pressed the alliance in warm terms.

sentences.zh: 且問備曰：「豫州今欲何至？

translations.literal: Moreover he asked Bei saying: “Lord of Yu Province, now where do you wish to go?
translations.idiomatic: He asked, “Lord Liu of Yu province, where are you bound?”

sentences.zh: 」備曰：「與蒼梧太守

translations.literal: ” Bei said: “With Cangwu grand administrator
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Bei said, “I mean to join the grand administrator of Cangwu,

sentences.zh: （吳臣）

translations.literal: (Wu Chen [variant graph])
translations.idiomatic: Some texts read the name as Wu Chen here.

sentences.zh: 〔吳巨〕有舊，欲往投之。

translations.literal: 〔Wu Ju〕 had old ties; I wish to go and throw myself to him.
translations.idiomatic: 〔Wu Ju〕—an old acquaintance—and seek refuge with him.”

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「孫討虜聰明仁惠，敬賢禮士，江表英豪，咸歸附之，已據有六郡，兵精糧多，足以立事。

translations.literal: ” Su said: “Sun the Bandit-Suppressor is clever, wise, benevolent, and kind; he respects worthies and honors gentlemen; heroes east of the river all attach to him; he already holds six commanderies; troops crack, grain abundant—enough to establish enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lu Su answered, “Sun Quan is wise and generous, honors men of talent, and holds six commanderies east of the Long River with strong troops and full granaries—enough to build an empire.”

sentences.zh: 今為君計，莫若遣腹心使自結於東，崇連和之好，共濟世業，而云欲投

translations.literal: Now for your lord I plan: nothing better than send a trusted envoy to bind yourself with the east, exalt joint alliance’s goodness, together aid the age’s enterprise—yet you say you wish to throw yourself to
translations.idiomatic: “Send a trusted man east to seal an alliance and share the work of the age—yet you speak of fleeing to

sentences.zh: （吳臣）

translations.literal: (Wu Chen)
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chen (variant),

sentences.zh: 〔吳巨〕，

translations.literal: 〔Wu Ju〕,
translations.idiomatic: 〔Wu Ju〕,

translations.literal: (chen ‘minister’ [variant for 巨])
translations.idiomatic: Some manuscripts write the second graph as chen instead of ju;

sentences.zh: 〔巨〕是凡人，偏在遠郡，行將為人所併，豈足託乎？

translations.literal: 〔Ju〕 is a common man, biased in a distant commandery; soon will be swallowed by others—how enough to entrust to?
translations.idiomatic: 〔Ju〕 is a mediocrity in a remote commandery about to be swallowed—can he be your refuge?”

sentences.zh: 」備大喜，進住鄂縣，即遣諸葛亮隨肅詣孫權，結同盟誓。〉

translations.literal: ” Bei greatly rejoiced; advanced and lodged at E County; immediately sent Zhuge Liang following Su to visit Sun Quan, tying alliance oaths.〉
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Bei was delighted, advanced to E county, and sent Zhuge Liang with Lu Su to Sun Quan to swear alliance.”

sentences.zh: 權遣周瑜、程普等水軍數萬，與先主并力，

translations.literal: Quan sent Zhou Yu, Cheng Pu, and others’ water forces several tens of thousands, with the Former Lord combining strength,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent Zhou Yu, Cheng Pu, and tens of thousands of sailors to join Liu Bei’s force,

sentences.zh: 〈江表傳曰：備從魯肅計，進住鄂縣之樊口。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions from Beyond the River says: Bei followed Lu Su’s plan; advanced and lodged at E County’s Fankou.
translations.idiomatic: The Traditions from Beyond the River adds that Liu Bei followed Lu Su’s advice and camped at Fankou in E county.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮詣吳未還，備聞曹公軍下，恐懼，日遣邏吏於水次候望權軍。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang had gone to Wu and not returned; Bei heard Lord Cao’s army was descending; fearful; daily sent patrol clerks at the water’s edge to watch for Quan’s army.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhuge Liang was still in Wu, Liu Bei heard Cao Cao was coming downriver and posted pickets along the shore to watch for Sun Quan’s fleet.

sentences.zh: 吏望見瑜船，馳往白備，備曰：「何以知

translations.literal: The clerk saw Yu’s boats; galloped to report to Bei; Bei said: “By what know
translations.idiomatic: When a scout sighted Zhou Yu’s ships and raced back, Liu Bei asked, “How do you know

translations.literal: (zhi [supplied pronoun])
translations.idiomatic: it

sentences.zh: 非青徐軍邪？

translations.literal: is not Qing-Xu army?”
translations.idiomatic: is not a Qingzhou or Xuzhou fleet?”

sentences.zh: 」吏對曰：「以船知之。

translations.literal: ” The clerk answered saying: “By the boats know it.
translations.idiomatic: ” The man said, “By the ships.”

sentences.zh: 」備遣人慰勞之。

translations.literal: ” Bei sent men to console and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Bei sent men with thanks.

sentences.zh: 瑜曰：「有軍任，不可得委署，儻能屈威，誠副其所望。

translations.literal: Yu said: “There is military duty; cannot be delegated; if you can bend your awesomeness, truly matches what is hoped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu answered that military duty kept him from leaving his post, but if Liu Bei would condescend to visit, it would meet his hopes.

sentences.zh: 」備謂關羽、張飛曰：「彼欲致我，我今自結託於東而不往，非同盟之意也。

translations.literal: ” Bei said to Guan Yu and Zhang Fei: “He wishes to summon me; I now myself bind entrustment with the east yet do not go—it is not alliance intent.
translations.idiomatic: ” He told Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, “He asks me to come; to refuse would break the spirit of alliance.”

sentences.zh: 」乃乘單舸往見瑜，問曰：「今拒曹公，深為得計。

translations.literal: ” Then riding a single skiff he went to see Yu, asking: “Now resisting Lord Cao, deeply is the right plan.
translations.idiomatic: ” He took a light boat to Zhou Yu and said, “Your plan to face Cao Cao is sound.”

sentences.zh: 戰卒有幾？

translations.literal: Battle soldiers—how many?
translations.idiomatic: How many fighting men do you have?”

sentences.zh: 」瑜曰：「三萬人。

translations.literal: ” Yu said: “Thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhou Yu said, “Thirty thousand.”

sentences.zh: 」備曰：「恨少。

translations.literal: ” Bei said: “I regret it is few.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Bei said, “That seems thin.”

sentences.zh: 」瑜曰：「此自足用，豫州但觀瑜破之。

translations.literal: ” Yu said: “This is self-sufficient to use; Lord of Yu Province only watch Yu break them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhou Yu answered, “They will suffice—watch me break Cao Cao’s host.”

sentences.zh: 」備欲呼魯肅等共會語，瑜曰：「受命不得妄委署，若欲見子敬，可別過之。

translations.literal: ” Bei wished to call Lu Su and others to meet together in talk; Yu said: “Having received orders I cannot recklessly delegate; if you wish to see Zijing, you may separately visit him.
translations.idiomatic: ” When Liu Bei asked to bring Lu Su into the parley, Zhou Yu refused: “I may not leave my post; see Zijing on your own if you wish.”

sentences.zh: 又孔明已俱來，不過三兩日到也。

translations.literal: Moreover Kongming has already come together; not more than two three days then he arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang is already on the way and should arrive within a few days.”

sentences.zh: 」備雖深愧異瑜，而心未許之能必破北軍也，故差池在後，將二千人與羽、飛俱，未肯係瑜，蓋為進退之計也。

translations.literal: ” Although Bei deeply marveled at Yu, in his heart he did not concede that he could surely break the northern army; therefore he hung back behind; leading two thousand men together with Yu and Fei; was unwilling to tie to Yu—covertly was a plan of advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Bei admired Zhou Yu yet doubted he could really crush Cao Cao, so he lagged behind with two thousand men under Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, keeping his distance as a hedge.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：劉備雄才，處必亡之地，告急於吳，而獲奔助，無緣復顧望江渚而懷後計。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: Liu Bei had heroic talent; situated in land sure to perish; cried urgent to Wu and obtained fleeing aid—there was no reason again to gaze at the river islets and harbor afterward plans.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng argues that Liu Bei, a man of heroic caliber cornered on the brink, who had begged Wu for rescue, would not have idled on the shore scheming how to hold back.

sentences.zh: 江表傳之言，當是吳人欲專美之辭。〉

translations.literal: The words of the Traditions from Beyond the River ought to be Wu people wishing to monopolize praise’s phrasing.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Traditions from Beyond the River sounds like Wu spin to steal all the credit.”

sentences.zh: 與曹公戰於赤壁，大破之，焚其舟船。

translations.literal: With Lord Cao they fought at Red Cliffs; greatly broke them; burned their boats and ships.
translations.idiomatic: They fought Cao Cao at Red Cliffs, shattered his fleet, and burned his ships.

sentences.zh: 先主與吳軍水陸並進，追到南郡，時又疾疫，北軍多死，曹公引歸。

translations.literal: The Former Lord with Wu’s army by water and land together advanced; pursued to Nan Commandery; at that time again plague; northern troops mostly died; Lord Cao led return.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei and the Wu forces pressed by land and water to Nan commandery; plague wasted the northern army, and Cao Cao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 〈江表傳曰：周瑜為南郡太守，分南岸地以給備。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions from Beyond the River says: Zhou Yu was grand administrator of Nan Commandery; divided south-bank land to give to Bei.
translations.idiomatic: The Traditions from Beyond the River says Zhou Yu, as grand administrator of Nan commandery, ceded the south bank to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 備別立營於油江口，改名為公安。

translations.literal: Bei separately set a camp at Youjiang mouth; changed the name to Gongan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei built a separate camp at the mouth of the You River and renamed the place Gongan.

sentences.zh: 劉表吏士見從北軍，多叛來投備。

translations.literal: Liu Biao’s clerks and soldiers who had followed the northern army for the most part rebelled and came to attach to Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Liu Biao’s men who had served the northern army deserted to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 備以瑜所給地少，不足以安民，

translations.literal: Bei because the land Yu gave was little, not enough to settle the people,
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei found Zhou Yu’s grant too small to settle his people,

translations.literal: (later [variant])
translations.idiomatic: Later,

sentences.zh: 〔復〕從權借荊州數郡。〉

translations.literal: 〔again〕 borrowed from Quan several commanderies of Jing Province.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〔again〕 borrowed several Jingzhou commanderies from Sun Quan.”

sentences.zh: 先主表琦為荊州刺史，又南征四郡。

translations.literal: The Former Lord memorialized Qi as inspector of Jing Province; again south campaigned four commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He had Liu Qi named inspector of Jingzhou, then marched south to conquer the four southern commanderies.

sentences.zh: 武陵太守金旋、長沙太守韓玄、桂陽太守趙範、零陵太守劉度皆降。

translations.literal: Grand administrators Jin Xuan of Wuling, Han Xuan of Changsha, Zhao Fan of Guiyang, Liu Du of Lingling all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The grand administrators Jin Xuan of Wuling, Han Xuan of Changsha, Zhao Fan of Guiyang, and Liu Du of Lingling all submitted.

sentences.zh: 〈《三輔決錄注》曰：金旋字元機，京兆人，歷位黃門郎，漢陽太守，徵拜議郎，遷中郎將，領武陵太守，為備所攻劫死。

translations.literal: 〈The Commentary on the Records of the Three Adjuncts says: Jin Xuan, courtesy name Yuanji, a man of Jingzhao; passed through posts as palace attendant, grand administrator of Hanyang, summoned as gentleman-adviser, promoted general of the gentlemen of the household, concurrently grand administrator of Wuling; attacked by Bei and died in the raid.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Records of the Three Adjuncts identifies Jin Xuan, courtesy Yuanji, of Jingzhao, who fell when Liu Bei attacked his commandery.

sentences.zh: 子禕，事見《魏武本紀》。〉

translations.literal: Son Yi; the affair is seen in the Basic Annals of Wei Wu.〉
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin Yi is treated in the annals of Cao Cao.”

sentences.zh: 廬江雷緒率部曲數萬口稽顙。

translations.literal: Lei Xu of Lujiang led retainers several tens of thousands of mouths and knocked forehead.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Xu of Lujiang brought tens of thousands of followers to kneel in submission.

sentences.zh: 琦病死，羣下推先主為荊州牧，治公安。

translations.literal: Qi died of illness; his subordinates pushed the Former Lord to be governor of Jing Province; administered Gongan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qi died, his officers raised Liu Bei to governor of Jingzhou with his seat at Gongan.

sentences.zh: 權稍畏之，進妹固好。

translations.literal: Quan gradually feared him; advanced a younger sister to firm friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan began to fear him and sent a younger sister to cement the tie.

sentences.zh: 先主至京見權，綢繆恩紀。

translations.literal: The Former Lord reached Jing to see Quan; they were intimate in kindness and ties.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei went to Moling to see Sun Quan, and the two drew close in friendship.

sentences.zh: 〈《山陽公載記》曰：備還，謂左右曰：「孫車騎長上短下，其難為下，吾不可以再見之。

translations.literal: 〈The Records Carried from the Duke of Shanyang says: when Bei returned, he said to those at his side: “Sun the General of Chariots and Cavalry is long above and short below; it is hard to be below him—I cannot again see him.
translations.idiomatic: The Records Carried from the Duke of Shanyang quotes Liu Bei on his return: “Sun Quan is built long in the torso and short in the legs—hard to work under; I will not face him again.”

sentences.zh: 」乃晝夜兼行。

translations.literal: ” Then day and night doubled march.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then pressed night and day on the road.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：魏書載劉備與孫權語，與蜀志述諸葛亮與權語正同。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi’s note: the Book of Wei records Liu Bei’s words with Sun Quan; it is exactly the same as the Shu Annals’ account of Zhuge Liang’s words with Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that the Book of Wei’s version of Liu Bei’s words to Sun Quan matches the Shu Annals’ version of Zhuge Liang’s words to Sun Quan word for word.

sentences.zh: 劉備未破魏軍之前，尚未與孫權相見，不得有此說。

translations.literal: Liu Bei before breaking Wei’s army had not yet met Sun Quan; he could not have had this saying.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei had not yet met Sun Quan before the defeat of Cao Cao’s army, so this remark cannot be authentic.

sentences.zh: 故知蜀志為是。〉

translations.literal: Therefore know the Shu Annals is correct.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Annals version is therefore to be trusted.”

sentences.zh: 權遣使云欲共取蜀，或以為宜報聽許，吳終不能越荊有蜀，蜀地可為己有。

translations.literal: Quan sent envoys saying he wished together to take Shu; some thought it fitting to answer and listen and permit; Wu in the end could not cross Jing to hold Shu; Shu land could become one’s own possession.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan proposed a joint strike on Shu, some advisers said to agree: Wu could never hold Shu across Jingzhou, so the west would fall to Liu Bei alone.

sentences.zh: 荊州主簿殷觀進曰：「若為吳先驅，進未能克蜀，退為吳所乘，即事去矣。

translations.literal: Jing Province registrar Yin Guan advanced saying: “If we become Wu’s vanguard, advancing unable to conquer Shu, withdrawing ridden by Wu—then the affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Guan, chief clerk of Jingzhou, objected: “If we spearhead Wu’s attack, fail to take Shu, and are caught from behind by Wu, all is lost.”

sentences.zh: 今但可然贊其伐蜀，而自說新據諸郡，未可興動，吳必不敢越我而獨取蜀。

translations.literal: Now we can only approve and praise their campaign against Shu, but ourselves explain newly holding the various commanderies, not yet able to raise movement; Wu surely will not dare cross us alone to take Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Praise their plan but plead that our new conquests are still unsettled and our troops cannot move; Wu will not dare march past us to seize Shu alone.”

sentences.zh: 如此進退之計，可以收吳、蜀之利。

translations.literal: Thus advance-and-retreat planning can gather Wu and Shu’s profit.
translations.idiomatic: That strategy secures the best of both Wu and Shu.”

sentences.zh: 」先主從之，權果輟計。

translations.literal: ” The Former Lord followed it; Quan indeed dropped the plan.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Bei took the counsel, and Sun Quan dropped the scheme.

sentences.zh: 遷觀為別駕從事。

translations.literal: Guan was promoted to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Guan was promoted to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝春秋》曰：孫權欲與備共取蜀，遣使報備曰：「米賊張魯居王巴、漢，為曹操耳目，規圖益州。

translations.literal: 〈The Springs and Autumns of Emperor Xian says: Sun Quan wished with Bei together to take Shu; sent envoys reporting to Bei saying: “The rice bandit Zhang Lu dwells kinglike in Ba and Han, is Cao Cao’s eyes and ears, plots to map Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Springs and Autumns of Emperor Xian records that Sun Quan proposed a joint invasion of Shu, writing to Liu Bei that the “rice-bandit” Zhang Lu held Ba and Hanzhong as Cao Cao’s outpost and aimed at Yizhou.”

sentences.zh: 劉璋不武，不能自守。

translations.literal: Liu Zhang is not martial; cannot guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang is no soldier and cannot defend himself.”

sentences.zh: 若操得蜀，則荊州危矣。

translations.literal: If Cao obtains Shu, then Jing Province is perilous.
translations.idiomatic: If Cao Cao takes Shu, Jingzhou is lost.”

sentences.zh: 今欲先攻取璋，進討張魯，首尾相連，一統吳、楚，雖有十操，無所憂也。

translations.literal: Now wishing first to attack and take Zhang, advance punish Zhang Lu, head and tail linked together, unify Wu and Chu—although there were ten Caos, there is nothing to worry.
translations.idiomatic: Let us strike Liu Zhang first, then Zhang Lu, link our fronts, and unite Wu and Chu—then ten Cao Caos would not trouble us.”

sentences.zh: 」備欲自圖蜀，拒答不聽，曰：〉

translations.literal: ” Bei wished himself to map Shu; refused answer would not listen; said:〉
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Bei meant to take Shu himself and declined, replying:”

sentences.zh: 益州民富彊，土地險阻，劉璋雖弱，足以自守。

translations.literal: Yizhou’s people are rich and strong; land is perilous and blocked; although Liu Zhang is weak, enough to guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou is rich, its terrain formidable; weak as Liu Zhang is, he can still hold it.

sentences.zh: 張魯虛偽，未必盡忠於操。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu is false and hollow; not necessarily wholly loyal to Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu is a charlatan and hardly Cao Cao’s loyal vassal.

sentences.zh: 今暴師於蜀、漢，轉運於萬里，欲使戰克攻取，舉不失利，此吳起不能定其規，孫武不能善其事也。

translations.literal: Now violently exposing the army in Shu and Han, transporting turnings at ten thousand li, wishing to make battle overcome and attack seize, every act without missing profit—this Wu Qi could not fix his plan, Sun Wu could not perfect his affair.
translations.idiomatic: To throw armies into Shu and Hanzhong and haul supplies a thousand miles, expecting every blow to land—Wu Qi could not draft such a plan, nor Sunzi carry it out.”

sentences.zh: 曹操雖有無君之心，而有奉主之名，議者見操失利於赤壁，謂其力屈，無復遠志也。

translations.literal: Although Cao Cao has a heart without lord, yet he has a name of serving the lord; debaters seeing Cao defeated at Red Cliffs, call his strength bent, no again distant ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao may disdain his sovereign yet still plays the loyal minister; men who saw him beaten at Red Cliffs think his strength spent and his ambitions local.”

sentences.zh: 今操三分天下已有其二，將欲飲馬於滄海，觀兵於吳會，何肯守此坐須老乎？

translations.literal: Now Cao two-thirds of the split realm already has two parts; will wish to water horses at the dark sea, display troops at Wu and Kuaiji—how willing guard here sitting until old?
translations.idiomatic: He holds two parts of three and means to water his horses in the sea and parade his hosts at Wu—will he sit idle until he grows old?”

sentences.zh: 今同盟無故自相攻伐，借樞於操，使敵承其隙，非長計也。

translations.literal: Now the allied bond without cause mutually attacks and strikes; lends the bolt to Cao; makes the enemy receive their crack—not a long plan.
translations.idiomatic: For allies to strike one another without cause hands Cao Cao the pivot and invites him through the breach—no lasting strategy.”

sentences.zh: 〈權不聽，遣孫瑜率水軍住夏口。

translations.literal: 〈Quan did not listen; sent Sun Yu to lead water army and stay at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan ignored him and sent Sun Yu with the fleet to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 備不聽軍過，謂瑜曰：「汝欲取蜀，吾當被髮入山，不失信於天下也。

translations.literal: Bei would not listen to the army passing; said to Yu: “You wish to take Shu; I shall let hair loose and enter the mountains—not lose trust in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei barred the march and told Sun Yu, “If you take Shu, I shall hide my hair in the hills rather than break faith with the world.”

sentences.zh: 」使關羽屯江陵，張飛屯秭歸，諸葛亮據南郡，備自住孱陵。

translations.literal: ” He made Guan Yu garrison Jiangling, Zhang Fei garrison Zigui, Zhuge Liang hold Nan Commandery; Bei himself dwelt at Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: ” He posted Guan Yu at Jiangling, Zhang Fei at Zigui, Zhuge Liang in Nan commandery, and himself at Yanling.

sentences.zh: 權知備意，因召瑜還。〉

translations.literal: Quan knew Bei’s intent; therefore summoned Yu back.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan read Liu Bei’s resolve and recalled Sun Yu.”

sentences.zh: 十六年，益州牧劉璋遙聞曹公將遣鍾繇等向漢中討張魯，內懷恐懼。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Yizhou Governor Liu Zhang from afar heard Lord Cao would send Zhong Yao and others toward Hanzhong to campaign against Zhang Lu; inwardly harbored fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an, Governor Liu Zhang of Yizhou heard from afar that Cao Cao would send Zhong Yao toward Hanzhong against Zhang Lu and was terrified.

sentences.zh: 別駕從事蜀郡張松說璋曰：「曹公兵強無敵於天下，若因張魯之資以取蜀土，誰能御之者乎？

translations.literal: Chief clerk Zhang Song of Shu Commandery persuaded Zhang saying: “Lord Cao’s troops are strong without peer under heaven; if by Zhang Lu’s resources he takes Shu soil, who can resist him?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song, chief clerk from Shu commandery, warned him, “Cao Cao’s army is unmatched; if he uses Zhang Lu as a bridge into Shu, who can stop him?”

sentences.zh: 」璋曰：「吾固憂之而未有計。

translations.literal: ” Zhang said: “I indeed worry it yet have no plan.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Zhang said, “I fear the same but see no plan.”

sentences.zh: 」松曰：「劉豫州，使君之宗室而曹公之深讎也，善用兵，若使之討魯，魯必破。

translations.literal: ” Song said: “Lord Liu of Yu Province is your excellency’s clansman and Lord Cao’s deep foe; good at using troops; if you make him punish Lu, Lu surely will be broken.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang Song answered, “Liu Bei is your kinsman and Cao Cao’s bitter enemy, and a fine soldier—send him against Zhang Lu and Zhang Lu will fall.”

sentences.zh: 魯破，則益州強，曹公雖來，無能為也。

translations.literal: When Lu is broken, then Yizhou is strong; although Lord Cao comes, he can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Crush Zhang Lu and Yizhou stands strong—Cao Cao can do nothing against you.”

sentences.zh: 」璋然之，遣法正將四千人迎先主，前後賂遺以巨億計。

translations.literal: ” Zhang approved it; sent Fa Zheng to lead four thousand men to welcome the Former Lord; before and after bribes and gifts counted in huge yi.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Zhang agreed, sent Fa Zheng with four thousand men to welcome Liu Bei, and lavished gifts worth billions in cash.

sentences.zh: 正因陳益州可取之策。

translations.literal: Zheng thereupon set forth the plan by which Yizhou could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng then laid out how Yizhou could be seized.

sentences.zh: 〈吳書曰：備前見張松，後得法正，皆厚以恩意接納，盡其殷勤之歡。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wu says: Bei earlier met Zhang Song; later obtained Fa Zheng; all thickly with kindness and intent received them; exhausted their earnest cordiality’s joy.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu says Liu Bei treated Zhang Song and Fa Zheng with lavish kindness and warm hospitality.

sentences.zh: 因問蜀中闊狹，兵器府庫人馬眾寡，及諸要害道里遠近，松等具言之，又畫地圖山川處所，由是盡知益州虛實也。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he asked Shu’s breadth and narrowness, weapons arsenals’ men and horses many or few, and the various key points’ road li far and near; Song and others fully told; also drew maps of mountains and rivers’ places; by this fully knew Yizhou’s emptiness and fullness.〉
translations.idiomatic: He questioned them on Shu’s roads, arsenals, troop counts, and strongpoints; they told all and sketched maps until he knew every weakness of Yizhou.”

sentences.zh: 先主留諸葛亮、關羽等據荊州，將步卒數万人入益州。

translations.literal: The Former Lord left Zhuge Liang, Guan Yu, and others to hold Jing Province; led infantry several tens of thousands into Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Zhuge Liang and Guan Yu to hold Jingzhou, he led several tens of thousands of foot into Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 至涪，璋自出迎，相見甚歡。

translations.literal: Reaching Fu, Zhang himself came out to welcome; meeting was very joyful.
translations.idiomatic: At Fu, Liu Zhang came out in person; their meeting was cordial.

sentences.zh: 張松令法正白先主，及謀臣龐統進說，便可於會所襲璋。

translations.literal: Zhang Song ordered Fa Zheng to report to the Former Lord; and counselor Pang Tong advanced persuasion—then could at the meeting place strike Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song had Fa Zheng and Pang Tong urge Liu Bei to seize Liu Zhang at the banquet.

sentences.zh: 先主曰：「此大事也，不可倉卒。

translations.literal: The Former Lord said: “This is a great matter; cannot be hasty.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord said, “That is too grave a step to rush.”

sentences.zh: 」璋推先主行大司馬，領司隸校尉；
