translations.literal: ” Zhang pushed the Former Lord to act as grand marshal, concurrently colonel director of retainers;
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Zhang named him acting grand marshal and colonel director of retainers;

sentences.zh: 先主亦推璋行鎮西大將軍，領益州牧。

translations.literal: the Former Lord also pushed Zhang to act as general-in-chief who guards the west, concurrently governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei in turn named Liu Zhang acting general-in-chief who guards the west and governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 璋增先主兵，使擊張魯，又令督白水軍。

translations.literal: Zhang increased the Former Lord’s troops, made him strike Zhang Lu, also ordered him supervise the Baishui army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang reinforced him and ordered him against Zhang Lu, putting him over the Baishui garrison.

sentences.zh: 先主並軍三萬餘人，車甲器械資貨甚盛。

translations.literal: The Former Lord combined armies more than thirty thousand men; chariots, armor, weapons, goods and supplies very abundant.
translations.idiomatic: His combined force passed thirty thousand, with wagons, armor, and stores in plenty.

sentences.zh: 是歲，璋還成都。

translations.literal: That year, Zhang returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Zhang returned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 先主北到葭萌，未即討魯，厚樹恩德，以收眾心。

translations.literal: The Former Lord north reached Jiameng; did not immediately punish Lu; thickly planted kindness and virtue to gather the host’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: North at Jiameng he delayed the campaign against Zhang Lu and piled up kindness to win hearts.

sentences.zh: 明年，曹公徵孫權，權呼先主自救。

translations.literal: The next year, Lord Cao campaigned against Sun Quan; Quan called the Former Lord to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Cao Cao attacked Sun Quan, who called on Liu Bei for rescue.

sentences.zh: 先主遣使告璋曰：「曹公徵吳，吳憂危急。

translations.literal: The Former Lord sent envoys telling Zhang: “Lord Cao campaigns against Wu; Wu worries peril is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sent word to Liu Zhang: “Cao Cao strikes Wu; Wu is in mortal peril.”

sentences.zh: 孫氏與孤本為脣齒，又樂進在青泥與關羽相拒，今不往救羽，進必大克，轉侵州界，其憂有甚於魯。

translations.literal: The Sun clan with I originally were lips and teeth; moreover Yue Jin at Qingni resists Guan Yu; now if we do not go save Yu, Jin surely will greatly overcome, turn and invade the province’s borders—the worry is greater than Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan and I are lip and tooth; Yue Jin faces Guan Yu at Qingni—if I do not go, Yue Jin will break through and ravage your borders worse than Zhang Lu ever could.”

sentences.zh: 魯自守之賊，不足慮也。

translations.literal: Lu is a self-guarding bandit; not enough to worry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu is a mere hedgehog—no cause for fear.”

sentences.zh: 」乃從璋求萬兵及資

translations.literal: ” Then from Zhang sought ten thousand troops and supplies
translations.idiomatic: ” He then asked Liu Zhang for ten thousand men and supplies

translations.literal: (treasure [variant for 資])
translations.idiomatic: Some texts add “treasure” here alongside supplies;

sentences.zh: ，欲以東行。

translations.literal: , wishing thereby to march east.
translations.idiomatic: intending to march east.”

sentences.zh: 璋但許兵四千，其餘皆給半。

translations.literal: Zhang only permitted four thousand troops; the rest all gave half.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang allowed only four thousand men and halved the rest of his request.

sentences.zh: 〈魏書曰：備因激怒其眾曰：「吾為益州徵強敵，師徒勤瘁，不遑寧居；

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei says: Bei thereby stirred anger in his host saying: “I for Yizhou campaign against a strong foe; army and followers toil and weary; no leisure to dwell in peace;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says he roused his troops: “I fight Yizhou’s enemies while my men wear themselves out without rest;

sentences.zh: 今積帑藏之財而吝於賞功，望士大夫為出死力戰，其可得乎！」〉

translations.literal: now hoarding treasury-stored wealth yet stingy in rewarding merit—hoping gentlemen will for you expend utmost strength in battle—how can it be obtained!”〉
translations.idiomatic: yet you hoard treasure and grudge rewards—do you think gentlemen will die for you?””

sentences.zh: 張松書與先主及法正曰：「今大事垂可立，如何釋此去乎！

translations.literal: Zhang Song wrote to the Former Lord and Fa Zheng saying: “Now the great matter hangs almost ready to stand—how release this and leave!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song wrote to Liu Bei and Fa Zheng, “Victory is within reach—how can you walk away now?”

sentences.zh: 」松兄廣漢太守肅，懼禍逮己，白璋發其謀。

translations.literal: ” Song’s elder brother, grand administrator of Guanghan Su, feared disaster reaching himself; reported to Zhang and exposed the plot.
translations.idiomatic: ” His brother Zhang Su, grand administrator of Guanghan, fearing ruin, informed Liu Zhang of the plot.

sentences.zh: 於是璋收斬松，嫌隙始構矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang seized and beheaded Song; suspicion’s crack began to be built.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang seized Zhang Song and had him executed, and the breach between them opened.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊雜記》曰：張肅有威儀，容貌甚偉。

translations.literal: 〈The Miscellaneous Records of the Elders of Yibu says: Zhang Su had awe-inspiring bearing; appearance very grand.
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Records of the Elders of Yibu describes Zhang Su as imposing in bearing and stature.

sentences.zh: 松為人短小，放蕩不治節操，然識達精果，有才幹。

translations.literal: Song as a person was short in stature, dissolute and not regulating integrity; yet insight reached, keen and decisive, had talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song was short, unruly, and lax in morals, yet shrewd, decisive, and able.

sentences.zh: 劉璋遣詣曹公，曹公不甚禮；

translations.literal: Liu Zhang sent him to visit Lord Cao; Lord Cao did not greatly treat with ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang once sent him to Cao Cao, who treated him coldly;

sentences.zh: 公主簿楊脩深器之，白公闢松，公不納。

translations.literal: the lord’s registrar Yang Xiu deeply valued him; reported to the lord to summon Song; the lord did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu, the registrar, thought highly of him and urged Cao Cao to employ him, but Cao Cao refused.

sentences.zh: 脩以公所撰兵書示松，松宴飲之間一看便闇誦。

translations.literal: Xiu with the lord’s composed military book showed Song; Song at banquet drinking’s interval one look then recited from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu showed him Cao Cao’s military treatise; at a banquet Zhang Song glanced once and recited it from memory.

sentences.zh: 脩以此益異之。〉

translations.literal: Xiu for this all the more marveled at him.〉
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu marveled at him all the more.”

sentences.zh: 璋敕關戍諸將文書勿複關通先主。

translations.literal: Zhang ordered pass garrison various generals’ documents not again to pass through to the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang ordered the frontier posts to cut all communication with Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 先主大怒，召璋白水軍督楊懷，責以無禮，斬之。

translations.literal: The Former Lord was greatly angry; summoned Zhang’s Baishui army supervisor Yang Huai; blamed him for lack of ritual; beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei in fury summoned Yang Huai, commander of the Baishui garrison, rebuked him for discourtesy, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 乃使黃忠、卓膺勒兵向璋。

translations.literal: Then he sent Huang Zhong, Zhuo Ying to bind troops toward Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Huang Zhong and Zhuo Ying against Liu Zhang.

sentences.zh: 先主徑至關中，質諸將並士卒妻子，引兵與忠、膺等進到涪，據其城。

translations.literal: The Former Lord went straight to within the pass; held hostage the various generals together with soldiers’ wives and children; led troops with Zhong, Ying, and others advanced to Fu; occupied its city.
translations.idiomatic: He marched straight into the pass, seized the officers and soldiers’ families as hostages, joined Huang Zhong and Zhuo Ying, and took Fu.

sentences.zh: 璋遣劉跂、冷苞、張任、鄧賢等拒先主於涪，

translations.literal: Zhang sent Liu Gui, Leng Bao, Zhang Ren, Deng Xian, and others to resist the Former Lord at Fu,
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang sent Liu Gui, Leng Bao, Zhang Ren, and Deng Xian to hold Liu Bei at Fu,

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊雜記》曰：張任，蜀郡人，家世寒門。

translations.literal: 〈The Miscellaneous Records of the Elders of Yibu says: Zhang Ren, a man of Shu Commandery; family generations cold gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Records of the Elders of Yibu names Zhang Ren of Shu commandery, from a humble house.

sentences.zh: 少有膽勇，有志節，仕州為從事。〉

translations.literal: In youth had gallantry and courage; had aspiration and integrity; served the province as clerk.〉
translations.idiomatic: Bold and high-minded from youth, he served the province as a clerk.”

sentences.zh: 皆破敗，退保綿竹。

translations.literal: All were broken and defeated; withdrew to guard Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: They were routed and fell back to Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 璋復遣李嚴督綿竹諸軍，嚴率眾降先主。

translations.literal: Zhang again sent Li Yan to supervise Mianzhu’s various armies; Yan led the host to surrender to the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang sent Li Yan to command the Mianzhu armies, but Li Yan came over with his troops to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 先主軍益強，分遣諸將平下屬縣，諸葛亮、張飛、趙雲等將兵溯流定白帝、江州、江陽，惟關羽留鎮荊州。

translations.literal: The Former Lord’s army grew stronger; separately dispatched various generals to pacify subordinate counties; Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun, and others led troops upstream to settle Baicheng, Jiangzhou, Jiangyang; only Guan Yu remained to guard Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His army swelled; he sent generals to pacify the counties while Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, and Zhao Yun moved upriver to secure Baicheng, Jiangzhou, and Jiangyang, leaving only Guan Yu to guard Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 先主進軍圍雒；

translations.literal: The Former Lord advanced the army and besieged Luo;
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to besiege Luoxian;

sentences.zh: 時璋子循守城，被攻且一年。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang’s son Xun guarded the city; was attacked nearly one year.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang’s son Liu Xun held the town under siege for nearly a year.

sentences.zh: 十九年夏，雒城破，

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year’s summer, Luocheng was broken,
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the nineteenth year of Jian'an, Luoxian fell,

sentences.zh: 〈益部耆舊雜記曰：劉璋遣張任、劉跂率精兵拒捍先主於涪，為先主所破，退與璋子循守雒城。

translations.literal: 〈The Miscellaneous Records of the Elders of Yibu says: Liu Zhang sent Zhang Ren, Liu Gui leading crack troops to resist and defend against the Former Lord at Fu; were broken by the Former Lord; withdrew together with Zhang’s son Xun to guard Luocheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Records of the Elders of Yibu says Liu Zhang sent Zhang Ren and Liu Gui with picked troops to hold Liu Bei at Fu; they were beaten and fell back with Liu Xun to defend Luoxian.

sentences.zh: 任勒兵出於雁橋，戰复敗。

translations.literal: Ren bound troops and went out at Wild Goose Bridge; again defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ren led his men out at Wild Goose Bridge and was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 禽任。

translations.literal: Captured Ren.
translations.idiomatic: They took Zhang Ren alive.

sentences.zh: 先主聞任之忠勇，令軍降之，任厲聲曰：「老臣終不復事二主矣。

translations.literal: The Former Lord heard of Ren’s loyalty and courage; ordered the army to make him surrender; Ren in stern voice said: “This old minister in the end will not again serve two lords.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei, admiring his loyalty and courage, ordered him spared if he yielded; Zhang Ren shouted, “An old servant does not serve two masters.”

sentences.zh: 」乃殺之。

translations.literal: ” Then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” So they executed him.

sentences.zh: 先主嘆惜焉。〉

translations.literal: The Former Lord sighed and pitied him.〉
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei mourned him.”

sentences.zh: 進圍成都數十日，璋出降。

translations.literal: Advancing he besieged Chengdu several tens of days; Zhang came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After many days’ siege of Chengdu, Liu Zhang came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：初，劉備襲蜀，丞相掾趙戩曰：「劉備其不濟乎？

translations.literal: 〈Master Fu’s Book says: at first, when Liu Bei raided Shu, Chancellor’s clerk Zhao Jian said: “Will Liu Bei not succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu’s Book records that when Liu Bei invaded Shu, Zhao Jian, a clerk in the chancellery, asked, “Will Liu Bei fail?”

sentences.zh: 拙於用兵，每戰則敗，奔亡不暇，何以圖人？

translations.literal: Clumsy in using troops; every battle then defeat; fleeing not leisure—how thereby map others?
translations.idiomatic: He is clumsy in war, loses every fight, and flees for his life—how can he conquer anyone?”

sentences.zh: 蜀雖小區，險固四塞，獨守之國，難卒並也。

translations.literal: Shu although a small region, perilous and firm with four blockages, a state that guards alone—hard suddenly to annex.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is small but ringed by passes; it is a state built to stand alone—not quickly swallowed.”

sentences.zh: 」徵士傅幹曰：「劉備寬仁有度，能得人死力。

translations.literal: ” Summoned gentleman Fu Gan said: “Liu Bei is lenient and benevolent with measure; able to make men expend utmost strength unto death.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu Gan answered, “Liu Bei is generous and measured; he can inspire men to die for him.”

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮達治知變，正而有謀，而為之相；

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang comprehends governance and knows change; upright yet has strategy; and acts as his chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang masters government and adapts to change, upright and resourceful as his chancellor;

sentences.zh: 張飛、關羽勇而有義，皆萬人之敵，而為之將：此三人者，皆人傑也。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei, Guan Yu brave yet have righteousness; all are a match for ten thousand men; and act as his generals: these three men are all human champions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei and Guan Yu are fearless and honorable, each a match for ten thousand, as his generals—these three are champions among men.”

sentences.zh: 以備之略，三傑佐之，何為不濟也？

translations.literal: With Bei’s strategy, three heroes assisting him—how act not succeed?
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Bei’s design and these three at his side, how could he fail?”

sentences.zh: 」《典略》曰：趙戩，字叔茂，京兆長陵人也。

translations.literal: ” The Compendium says: Zhao Jian, courtesy name Shumao, a man of Changling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Compendium identifies Zhao Jian, courtesy Shumao, of Changling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 質而好學，言稱詩書，愛卹於人，不論疏密。

translations.literal: Plain yet fond of learning; speech invoked the Odes and Documents; loved pity toward people, not discussing distant or close.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain, studious, quoted the classics, and showed kindness to all alike.

sentences.zh: 闢公府，入為尚書選部郎。

translations.literal: Summoned to the duke’s office; entered as gentleman of the Masters of Writing selection bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the duke’s bureau and became a gentleman of the Masters of Writing in the appointments section.

sentences.zh: 董卓欲以所私並充臺閣，戩拒不聽。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo wished with his private favorites together to fill the terraces and pavilions; Jian refused and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo tried to pack the ministries with his creatures, Zhao Jian refused.

sentences.zh: 卓怒，召戩欲殺之，觀者皆為戩懼，而戩自若。

translations.literal: Zhuo was angry; summoned Jian wishing to kill him; onlookers all for Jian feared, yet Jian was self-composed.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo raged and called for his death; the crowd trembled for him, but he stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 及見卓，引辭正色，陳說是非，卓雖凶戾，屈而謝之遷平陵令。

translations.literal: When he saw Zhuo, he drew phrases with correct color, set forth right and wrong; although Zhuo was fierce and cruel, bent and apologized to him, transferred him as magistrate of Pingling.
translations.idiomatic: Face to face he spoke with stern rectitude; even Dong Zhuo yielded and apologized, then named him magistrate of Pingling.

sentences.zh: 故將王允被害，莫敢近者，戩棄官收斂之。

translations.literal: Former general Wang Yun was harmed; none dared approach; Jian cast office and gathered and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yun was slain and no one dared approach the body, Zhao Jian resigned his post to bury him.

sentences.zh: 三輔亂，戩客荊州，劉表以為賓客。

translations.literal: The Three Adjuncts in chaos; Jian sojourned in Jing Province; Liu Biao made him a guest retainer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Adjuncts fell into chaos he fled to Jingzhou, where Liu Biao kept him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 曹公平荊州，執戩手曰：「何相見之晚也！

translations.literal: Lord Cao pacified Jing Province; grasped Jian’s hand saying: “Why meet so late!
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao took Jingzhou he took Zhao Jian’s hand and cried, “Why only now?”

sentences.zh: 」遂闢為掾。

translations.literal: ” Then summoned him as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: ” and appointed him a clerk.

sentences.zh: 後為五官將司馬，相國鍾繇長史，年六十餘卒。〉

translations.literal: Later became major to the General of the Household for All Five Purposes, minister Zhong Yao’s chief clerk; in his sixties-plus died.〉
translations.idiomatic: He later served as major to the heir apparent and chief clerk to Minister Zhong Yao, and died in his sixties.”

sentences.zh: 蜀中殷盛豐樂，先主置酒大饗士卒，取蜀城中金銀分賜將士，還其穀帛。

translations.literal: Within Shu was prosperous abundance and rich joy; the Former Lord set wine and greatly feasted soldiers and troops; took Shu city’s gold and silver divided and bestowed on generals and officers; returned its grain and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was rich and at peace; Liu Bei feasted his army, shared Chengdu’s gold and silver among the ranks, and returned grain and cloth to the people.

sentences.zh: 先主复領益州牧，諸葛亮為股肱，法正為謀主，關羽、張飛、馬超為爪牙，許靖、麋竺、簡雍為賓友。

translations.literal: The Former Lord again concurrently held governor of Yizhou; Zhuge Liang as thigh and arm; Fa Zheng as planning master; Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Ma Chao as claws and fangs; Xu Jing, Mi Zhu, Jian Yong as guest friends.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei again took the title governor of Yizhou, naming Zhuge Liang and Fa Zheng his right and left hands, Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, and Ma Chao his claws, and Xu Jing, Mi Zhu, and Jian Yong his counselors.

sentences.zh: 及董和、黃權、李嚴等本璋之所授用也，吳壹、費觀等又璋之婚親也，彭羕又璋之所排擯也，劉巴者宿昔之所忌恨也，皆處之顯任，盡其器能。

translations.literal: As for Dong He, Huang Quan, Li Yan and others—they were originally those Zhang employed; Wu Yi, Fei Guan and others moreover were Zhang’s marriage kin; Peng Yang moreover was one Zhang pushed aside; Liu Ba was one long hated in the past—all were placed in eminent posts, exhausted their vessels and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Dong He, Huang Quan, Li Yan, and others whom Liu Zhang had employed, Wu Yi and Fei Guan who were his in-laws, Peng Yang whom he had spurned, and Liu Ba whom he had feared—all received high office suited to their talents.

sentences.zh: 有誌之士，無不競勸。

translations.literal: Those with aspiration’s gentlemen; none did not compete in encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Men of ambition strove harder than ever.

sentences.zh: 二十年，孫權以先主已得益州，使使報欲得荊州。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Sun Quan because the Former Lord had already obtained Yizhou, sent envoys reporting wishing to obtain Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Jian'an, Sun Quan sent envoys to demand Jingzhou now that Liu Bei held Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 先主言：「須得涼州，當以荊州相與。

translations.literal: The Former Lord said: “Must obtain Liang Province; then will give Jing Province to you.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei answered, “When I have Liangzhou, I will give you Jingzhou.”

sentences.zh: 」權忿之，乃遣呂蒙襲奪長沙、零陵、桂陽三郡。

translations.literal: ” Quan was angry at it; then sent Lu Meng to raid and seize Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Quan in fury sent Lu Meng to seize Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 先主引兵五萬下公安，令關羽入益陽。

translations.literal: The Former Lord led troops fifty thousand down to Gongan; ordered Guan Yu to enter Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei brought fifty thousand men to Gongan and ordered Guan Yu into Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，曹公定漢中，張魯遁走巴西。

translations.literal: That year, Lord Cao pacified Hanzhong; Zhang Lu fled and went to Ba in the west.
translations.idiomatic: That year Cao Cao took Hanzhong and Zhang Lu fled into Bazhong.

sentences.zh: 先主聞之，與權連和，分荊州、江夏、長沙、桂陽東屬，南郡、零陵、武陵西屬，引軍還江州。

translations.literal: The Former Lord heard it; with Quan linked peace; divided Jingzhou, Jiangxia, Changsha, Guiyang east attached; Nan Commandery, Lingling, Wuling west attached; led army back to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Liu Bei made peace with Sun Quan: Jiangxia, Changsha, and Guiyang went east to Wu; Nan commandery, Lingling, and Wuling stayed with him, and he withdrew to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣黃權將兵迎張魯，張魯已降曹公。

translations.literal: He sent Huang Quan to lead troops to welcome Zhang Lu; Zhang Lu had already surrendered to Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Huang Quan to meet Zhang Lu, but Zhang Lu had already surrendered to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 曹公使夏侯淵、張郃屯漢中，數數犯暴巴界。

translations.literal: Lord Cao made Xiahou Yuan, Zhang He garrison Hanzhong; repeatedly repeatedly violated and ravaged Ba’s borders.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao posted Xiahou Yuan and Zhang He in Hanzhong, and they raided Ba again and again.

sentences.zh: 先主令張飛進兵宕渠，與郃等戰於瓦口，破郃等，收兵還南鄭。

translations.literal: The Former Lord ordered Zhang Fei to advance troops to Dangqu; with He and others fought at Wakou; broke He and others; gathered troops and returned to Nan Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sent Zhang Fei to Dangqu, defeated Zhang He at Wakou, and drove him back to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 先主亦還成都。

translations.literal: The Former Lord also returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei returned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，先主率諸將進兵漢中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the Former Lord led the various generals advancing troops into Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he led his generals into Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 分遣將軍吳蘭、雷銅等入武都，皆為曹公軍所沒。

translations.literal: Separately dispatched generals Wu Lan, Lei Tong, and others into Wudu; all were swallowed by Lord Cao’s army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wu Lan and Lei Tong into Wudu, but Cao Cao’s forces destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 先主次於陽平關，與淵、郃等相拒。

translations.literal: The Former Lord halted at Yangping Pass; with Yuan, He, and others faced each other in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: He camped at Yangping Pass against Xiahou Yuan and Zhang He.

sentences.zh: 二十四年春，自陽平南渡沔水，緣山稍前，於定軍山勢作營。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year’s spring, from Yangping south crossed Mian water; along the mountain gradually advanced; on Dingjun Mountain’s slope made camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year he crossed the Mian south from Yangping, worked along the heights, and camped on Dingjun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 淵將兵來爭其地。

translations.literal: Yuan led troops to contest that ground.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Yuan marched to dispute the ground.

sentences.zh: 先主命黃忠乘高鼓譟攻之，大破淵軍，斬淵及曹公所署益州刺史趙顒等。

translations.literal: The Former Lord ordered Huang Zhong to ride the height, drum and clamor, attack them; greatly broke Yuan’s army; beheaded Yuan and Lord Cao’s appointed Yizhou Inspector Zhao Yong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei ordered Huang Zhong to charge downhill with drums and shouts, shattered Xiahou Yuan’s army, and slew Yuan and Cao Cao’s appointee as inspector of Yizhou, Zhao Yong, among others.

sentences.zh: 曹公自長安舉眾南征。

translations.literal: Lord Cao from Chang’an raised the host on a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then marched south from Chang’an at the head of a great host.

sentences.zh: 先主遙策之曰：「曹公雖來，無能為也，我必有漢川矣。

translations.literal: The Former Lord from afar divined saying: “Although Lord Cao comes, he can do nothing; I am sure to have the Han rivers.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei predicted, “Even if Cao Cao comes, he can do nothing—I shall hold the Han basin.”

sentences.zh: 」及曹公至，先主斂眾拒險，終不交鋒，積月不拔，亡者日多。

translations.literal: ” When Lord Cao arrived, the Former Lord gathered the host and resisted at narrows; to the end did not cross spears; piled months could not extract; deserters daily many.
translations.idiomatic: ” When Cao Cao arrived, Liu Bei drew up on the defiles and refused battle for months until desertions mounted in Cao’s camp.

sentences.zh: 夏，曹公果引軍還，先主遂有漢中。

translations.literal: In summer, Lord Cao indeed led the army back; the Former Lord then had Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Cao Cao withdrew, and Liu Bei took Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 遣劉封、孟達、李平等攻申耽於上庸。

translations.literal: He sent Liu Feng, Meng Da, Li Ping, and others to attack Shen Dan at Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Feng, Meng Da, and Li Ping against Shen Dan at Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 秋，群下上先主為漢中王，表於漢帝曰：

translations.literal: In autumn, his subordinates memorialized upward the Former Lord as King of Hanzhong, memorial to the Han emperor saying:
translations.idiomatic: That autumn his officers petitioned to have him named king of Hanzhong, addressing the memorial to the Han emperor:

sentences.zh: 平西將軍都亭侯臣馬超、左將軍

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West village marquis subject Ma Chao, General of the Left
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Ma Chao, general who pacifies the west and village marquis of Duting; the general of the left

translations.literal: (concurrently holding [variant])
translations.idiomatic: Some texts add “concurrently” here before the next titles;

sentences.zh: 長史鎮軍將軍臣許靖、營司馬臣龐羲、議曹從事中郎軍議中郎將臣射援、

translations.literal: Chief clerk General Who Guards the Army subject Xu Jing, camp major subject Pang Xi, consult bureau attendant clerk army consult middle general subject She Yuan,
translations.idiomatic: chief clerk and general who guards the army Xu Jing; camp major Pang Xi; attendant of the consult bureau and army discussant She Yuan;

sentences.zh: 〈三輔決錄注曰：援字文雄，扶風人也。

translations.literal: 〈The Commentary on the Records of the Three Adjuncts says: Yuan’s courtesy name Wenxiong, a man of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Records of the Three Adjuncts gives She Yuan, courtesy Wenxiong, of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 其先本姓謝，與北地諸謝同族。

translations.literal: His ancestors originally surnamed Xie, with Beidi’s various Xie same clan.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were surnamed Xie and kin to the Xie of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 始祖謝服為將軍出征，天子以謝服非令名，改為射，子孫氏焉。

translations.literal: First ancestor Xie Fu as general went on campaign; the Son of Heaven because Xie Fu was not a fine name, changed to She; descendants took it as surname.
translations.idiomatic: The founder Xie Fu took the field as a general; the emperor disliked the name and changed it to She, which his line adopted.

sentences.zh: 兄堅，字文固，少有美名，闢公府為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Elder brother Jian, courtesy name Wengu; in youth had fair name; summoned to duke’s office as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother She Jian, courtesy Wengu, famed in youth, served as palace attendant in the duke’s bureau.

sentences.zh: 獻帝之初，三輔飢亂，堅去官，與弟援南入蜀依劉璋，璋以堅為長史。

translations.literal: At Emperor Xian’s beginning, the Three Adjuncts were hungry and chaotic; Jian left office; together with younger brother Yuan south entered Shu to rely on Liu Zhang; Zhang made Jian chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xian’s reign, when the Three Adjuncts starved in chaos, She Jian resigned and with his brother She Yuan fled south to Liu Zhang, who named Jian chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 劉備代璋，以堅為廣漢、蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: Liu Bei replaced Zhang; made Jian grand administrator of Guanghan and Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei replaced Liu Zhang, he made She Jian grand administrator of Guanghan and Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 援亦少有名行，太尉皇甫嵩賢其才而以女妻之，丞相諸葛亮以援為祭酒，遷從事中郎，卒官。〉

translations.literal: Yuan also in youth had name and conduct; Grand Commandant Huangfu Song deemed his talent worthy and gave him a daughter as wife; Chancellor Zhuge Liang made Yuan libationer; promoted attendant clerk; died in office.〉
translations.idiomatic: She Yuan too was known in youth for character; Huangfu Song married him a daughter for his talent; Zhuge Liang made him libationer, then attendant clerk, and he died in office.”

sentences.zh: 軍師將軍臣諸葛亮、蕩寇將軍漢壽亭侯臣關羽、徵虜將軍新亭侯臣張飛、征西將軍臣黃忠、鎮遠將軍臣賴恭、揚武將軍臣法正、興業將軍臣李嚴等一百二十人上言曰：昔唐堯至聖而四凶在朝，周成仁賢而四國作難，高後稱製而諸呂竊命，孝昭幼衝而上官逆謀，皆馮世寵，藉履國權，窮凶極亂，社稷幾危。

translations.literal: General of the Army subject Zhuge Liang, General Who Sweeps the Bandits Hanshou village marquis subject Guan Yu, General Who Captures Caitiffs Xinting marquis subject Zhang Fei, General of the West subject Huang Zhong, General Who Guards the Distance subject Lai Gong, General Who Displays Martial Might subject Fa Zheng, General Who Establishes Enterprise subject Li Yan and others one hundred twenty persons upward speak saying: Formerly Tang Yao was supremely sage yet four villains were at court; Zhou Cheng was benevolent and worthy yet four states made difficulty; Empress Gao assumed regency yet the various Lüs stole the mandate; Emperor Xiaozhao was young and tender yet Shangguan plotted rebellion—all rode age’s favor, trod state power, exhausted villainy and utmost chaos; the altars of soil and grain nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects Zhuge Liang, general of the army; Guan Yu, general who sweeps the bandits and marquis of Hanshou village; Zhang Fei, general who captures caitiffs and marquis of Xinting; Huang Zhong, general of the west; Lai Gong, general who guards the distance; Fa Zheng, general who displays martial might; Li Yan, general who establishes enterprise; and one hundred twenty others memorialize: In antiquity Emperor Yao was supremely sage, yet four villains sat in court; King Cheng of Zhou was benevolent and worthy, yet four states rose in rebellion; Empress Lü held the regency, yet the Lü clan usurped the mandate; Emperor Zhao of Han was a minor, yet the Shangguans plotted treason—all rode favor, seized power, ran to extremes of evil, and brought the altars of state to the brink of ruin.

sentences.zh: 非大舜、周公、硃虛、博陸，則不能流放禽討，安危定傾。

translations.literal: Were it not for great Shun, the Duke of Zhou, Zhu-Xu, and Bolu, then could not banish, cage, and punish, settle danger and fix the overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Only a Shun, a Duke of Zhou, a Liu Zhang of Zhu-Xu, or a Huo Guang of Bolu could banish the wicked, cage the rebels, steady the peril, and right the fallen state.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下誕姿聖德，統理萬邦，而遭厄運不造之艱。

translations.literal: We prostrate ourselves: Your Majesty was born with sage virtue, orders and governs the myriad regions, yet meets ill fate and mis-created hardship.
translations.idiomatic: We prostrate ourselves before Your Majesty, born with sage virtue to rule the myriad regions, yet caught in misfortune and untimely hardship.

sentences.zh: 董卓首難，盪覆京畿，曹操階禍，竊執天衡；

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo first raised disaster, overturned the capital region; Cao Cao mounted on misfortune, secretly grasped Heaven’s steelyard;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo began the catastrophe and overturned the capital; Cao Cao climbed on calamity and seized the levers of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 皇后太子，鴆殺見害，剝亂天下，殘毀民物。

translations.literal: Empress and heir apparent were poison-killed and seen harmed; stripped and disordered the realm; maimed and destroyed the people’s things.
translations.idiomatic: he murdered empress and crown prince by poison, tore the realm apart, and laid waste to the people.

sentences.zh: 久令陛下蒙塵憂厄，幽處虛邑。

translations.literal: Long made Your Majesty endure dust and sorrowful peril, confined in an empty town.
translations.idiomatic: For long he has kept Your Majesty in exile and sorrow, imprisoned in an empty town.

sentences.zh: 人神無主，遏絕王命，厭昧皇極，欲盜神器。

translations.literal: Men and spirits lacked a lord; blocked and cut off the king’s commands; concealed the imperial extreme; wished to steal the sacred vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Men and spirits had no true lord; he choked off the royal command, veiled the throne, and meant to steal the regalia.

sentences.zh: 左將軍領司隸校尉豫、荊、益三州牧宜城亭侯備，受朝爵秩，念在輸力，以殉國難。

translations.literal: Left General concurrently Colonel Director of Retainers and shepherd of Yu, Jing, and Yi three provinces Yicheng village marquis Bei, having received court rank and stipend, thought to convey strength, to die for the state’s hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei, left general, colonel director of retainers, and shepherd of Yu, Jing, and Yi, marquis of Yicheng village, having received court rank, meant to spend his strength and die for the state in its peril.

sentences.zh: 睹其機兆，赫然憤發，與車騎將軍董承同謀誅操，將安國家，克寧舊都。

translations.literal: Seeing its omens and signs, blazingly roused in anger, with General of Chariots and Cavalry Dong Cheng together plotted to execute Cao, meaning to settle the state and family, be able to quiet the old capital.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the signs, he rose in wrath with General of chariots and cavalry Dong Cheng to put Cao Cao to death, meaning to restore the state and the old capital.

sentences.zh: 會承機事不密，令操遊魂得遂長惡，殘泯海內。

translations.literal: It happened Cheng’s affair was not secret; made Cao’s wandering soul able to lengthen evil, maim and extinguish within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng’s plot leaked, letting that roaming wraith prolong his crimes and ravage the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣等每懼王室大有閻樂之禍，小有定安之變，

translations.literal: We your servants always fear the royal house may have great Yan Le’s disaster, small Ding’an’s change,
translations.idiomatic: We ever fear for the house of Han a disaster like Yan Le’s murder of the Second Emperor or a shift like Wang Mang’s reduction of the infant duke of Ding’an,

sentences.zh: 〈趙高使閻樂殺二世。

translations.literal: 〈Zhao Gao made Yan Le kill the Second Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: Zhao Gao had Yan Le kill the Second Emperor of Qin.

sentences.zh: 王莽廢孺子以為定安公。〉

translations.literal: Wang Mang deposed the infant and made him duke of Ding’an.〉
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang deposed the infant emperor and named him duke of Ding’an.”

sentences.zh: 夙夜惴惴，戰栗累息。

translations.literal: Morning and night fearful and trembling, shuddering piled sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Night and day we tremble and dare not breathe.

sentences.zh: 昔在虞書，敦序九族，週監二代，封建同姓，詩著其義，歷載長久。

translations.literal: Formerly in the canon of Yu, thickly ordered the nine kin; Zhou looked to two generations, enfeoffed same surname; the Odes set forth its meaning; passed ages long enduring.
translations.idiomatic: The canon of Yu teaches kindness to kin; Zhou looked to the two previous dynasties and enfeoffed princes of its own blood; the Odes praise this, and it endured for ages.

sentences.zh: 漢興之初，割裂疆土，尊王子弟，是以卒折諸呂之難，而成太宗之基。

translations.literal: At Han’s rise’s beginning, carved and split territory, honored king sons and younger brothers; thereby in the end broke the various Lüs’ difficulty, and completed Taizong’s foundation.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose it carved out domains for imperial princes, and so in the end broke the Lü clan’s grip and laid the foundation for Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 臣等以備肺腑枝葉，宗子籓翰，心存國家，念在弭亂。

translations.literal: We consider Bei lung and viscera branch and leaf, cadet son screen and shaft; heart stores the state, thought rests in quelling chaos.
translations.idiomatic: We hold Liu Bei a kinsman of the imperial house, a cadet shield of the line—his heart is the state, his aim is to end rebellion.

sentences.zh: 自操破於漢中，海內英雄望風蟻附，而爵號不顯，九錫未加，非所以鎮衛社稷，光昭萬世也。

translations.literal: Since Cao was broken at Hanzhong, within-the-seas heroes at wind looked ant-attached; yet rank and title are not illustrious, nine bestowals not yet added—not the means thereby to guard and defend the altars of soil and grain, brighten and shine ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Since Cao Cao’s defeat at Hanzhong, heroes across the realm have rallied like ants to him, yet his titles do not match his merit and the nine honors have not been granted—this is no way to guard the altars or shine for ages.

sentences.zh: 奉辭在外，禮命斷絕。

translations.literal: Bearing phrases outside, ritual commands are cut off.
translations.idiomatic: We bear our charge beyond the capital while court orders cannot reach us.

sentences.zh: 昔河西太守梁統等值漢中興，限於山河，位同權均，不能相率，咸推竇融以為元帥，卒立效績，摧破隗囂。

translations.literal: Formerly west-of-the-River grand administrator Liang Tong and others met Han’s middle revival, limited by mountains and rivers, positions equal power balanced, could not lead one another; all pushed Dou Rong to be commander-in-chief; in the end established merit and performance, crushed and broke Wei Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose again, Liang Tong and the western governors, cut off by mountains and rivers and equal in rank, could not act in concert until they made Dou Rong supreme commander, won success, and destroyed Wei Xiao.

sentences.zh: 今社稷之難，急於隴、蜀。

translations.literal: Now the altars of soil and grain’s hardship is more urgent than Long or Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The peril to the altars is more urgent than it was in Longxi or Ba–Shu.

sentences.zh: 操外吞天下，內殘群寮，朝廷有蕭牆之危，而御侮未建，可為寒心。

translations.literal: Cao without swallows the realm; within maims the host of officials; the court has inner-wall’s peril, yet defense against insult is not established—can be heart-chilling.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao devours the realm without and maims the ministers within; the court faces peril within its own walls while no champion is raised—it chills the heart.

sentences.zh: 臣等輒依舊典，封備漢中王，拜大司馬，董齊六軍，糾合同盟，掃滅凶逆。

translations.literal: We rashly follow old precedent, enfeoff Bei King of Hanzhong, appoint Grand Marshal, oversee and align six armies, bind and join covenant allies, sweep and destroy fierce rebels.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore follow ancient precedent to enfeoff Liu Bei as king of Hanzhong, appoint him grand marshal, put the six armies in order, rally the covenant, and sweep away the traitors.

sentences.zh: 以漢中、巴、蜀、廣漢、犍為為國，所署置依漢初諸侯王故典。

translations.literal: Taking Hanzhong, Ba, Shu, Guanghan, and Qianwei as state; what is appointed and placed follows Han beginning feudal princes’ old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: His domain shall be Hanzhong, Ba, Shu, Guanghan, and Qianwei, with appointments as under the early Han kings.

sentences.zh: 夫權宜之製，苟利社稷，專之可也。

translations.literal: As for expedient measure’s system, if it profits the altars of soil and grain, to monopolize it is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Expedient acts that serve the altars may be taken on one’s own authority.

sentences.zh: 然後功成事立，臣等退伏矯罪，雖死無恨。

translations.literal: Then when merit is achieved and affair established, we your servants withdraw and submit to presumption’s guilt; although die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: When the deed is done we shall withdraw and accept punishment for presumption, and die without regret.

sentences.zh: 遂於沔陽設壇場，陳兵列眾，群臣陪位，讀奏訖，禦王冠於先主。

translations.literal: Then at Mianyang they set altar ground, arrayed troops and lined hosts; the host of ministers accompanied positions; finished reading the memorial; placed the king’s crown on the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: At Mianyang they built an altar, drew up the host, and the ministers took their places; when the memorial had been read, they set the king’s crown on Liu Bei’s head.

sentences.zh: 先主上言漢帝曰：

translations.literal: The Former Lord upward spoke to the Han emperor saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord addressed the Han emperor:

sentences.zh: 臣以具臣之才，荷上將之任，董督三軍，奉辭於外，不得掃除寇難，靖匡王室，久使陛下聖教陵遲，六合之內，否而未泰，惟憂反側，疢如疾首。

translations.literal: Your subject with a mere subject’s talent bears a supreme general’s charge, oversees and supervises three armies, bears phrases without, cannot sweep away bandit hardship, quiet and correct the royal house; long makes Your Majesty’s sage teaching decline and delay; within the six directions, blocked and not yet peaceful; only worry tossing and turning; sickness like aching head.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, with the talent of a mere placeholder, bears a supreme commander’s charge and leads the three armies beyond the capital, yet cannot sweep away the rebels or restore the royal house. For long Your Majesty’s sagely teaching has waned; within the six directions all is blocked and unquiet; I toss on my couch in grief as if my head would split.

sentences.zh: 曩者董卓造為亂階，自是之後，群凶縱橫，殘剝海內。

translations.literal: Formerly Dong Zhuo made rebellion’s steps; from this afterward, a pack of villains ranged at will, maimed and stripped within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Dong Zhuo opened the road to chaos; since then villains have run wild and torn the realm apart.

sentences.zh: 賴陛下聖德威靈，人神同應，或忠義奮討，或上天降罰，暴逆並殪，以漸冰消。

translations.literal: Relying on Your Majesty’s sage virtue awesome numen, men and spirits together responded; some by loyalty and righteousness rose to punish; some by Heaven above sent down punishment; violent rebels together perished, by degrees like ice melting.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Your Majesty’s sage virtue and awesome spirit, men and gods answered together: some rose in loyal wrath, some Heaven struck down, until the rebels perished like thawing ice.

sentences.zh: 惟獨曹操，久未梟除，侵擅國權，恣心極亂。

translations.literal: Only Cao Cao, long not yet owl-removed, encroaches and monopolizes state power, indulges heart in utmost chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Only Cao Cao remains unexecuted, usurping state power and running to the utmost of villainy.

sentences.zh: 臣昔與車騎將軍董承圖謀討操，機事不密，承見陷害，臣播越失據，忠義不果。

translations.literal: Your subject formerly with General of Chariots and Cavalry Dong Cheng plotted to punish Cao; the affair was not secret; Cheng was seen harmed; your subject was scattered and lost footing; loyalty and righteousness did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject once plotted with General Dong Cheng to destroy Cao Cao; the secret leaked, Dong Cheng was destroyed, and your subject was driven wandering, unable to fulfill his loyal duty.

sentences.zh: 遂得使操窮凶極逆，主後戮殺，皇子鴆害。

translations.literal: Thereby was able to make Cao exhaust villainy and utmost rebellion; lord and empress were slaughter-killed; imperial sons were poison-harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Cao Cao ran to extremes of evil, murdered empress and consorts, and poisoned the imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 雖糾合同盟，念在奮力，懦弱不武，歷年未效。

translations.literal: Although bound covenant allies, thought to exert strength, weak and not martial, passed years without effect.
translations.idiomatic: Though I rallied the covenant and meant to strike with all my strength, my weakness in arms has brought no success in years.

sentences.zh: 常恐殞沒，孤負國恩，寤寐永嘆，夕惕若厲。

translations.literal: Always fear perishing and sinking, alone betray state grace; waking and sleeping long sigh; evening fear as if whetstone.
translations.idiomatic: I ever fear death before my duty is done, betraying the state’s kindness; I sigh waking and sleeping and tremble at night as on a grinding stone.

sentences.zh: 今臣群寮以為在昔虞書敦敘九族，庶明勵翼，

translations.literal: Now your subject’s host of colleagues consider that in the past the canon of Yu thickly ordered the nine kin, the many bright ones encouraged wings,
translations.idiomatic: Now my colleagues cite the canon of Yu on ordering the nine branches of the kin and the many bright assistants who winged the throne,

sentences.zh: 〈鄭玄注曰：庶，眾也；

translations.literal: 〈Zheng Xuan’s commentary says: shu means ‘many’;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses: shu means ‘the many’;

sentences.zh: 勵，作也；

translations.literal: Li means ‘to act’;
translations.idiomatic: Li means ‘to act’;

sentences.zh: 敘，次序也。

translations.literal: Xu means sequence and order.
translations.idiomatic: Xu means ‘to put in order’.

sentences.zh: 序九族而親之，以眾明作羽翼之臣也。〉

translations.literal: Order the nine kin and draw them near; with the many bright ones act as wing-feather ministers.〉
translations.idiomatic: Order the nine branches of the kin and cherish them, and let the many worthy men serve as wings to the throne.”

sentences.zh: 五帝損益，此道不廢。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors diminished and increased; this way was not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Five Emperors’ ages of wax and wane, this principle never failed.

sentences.zh: 週監二代，並建諸姬，實賴晉、鄭夾輔之福。

translations.literal: Zhou looked to two generations; together established the various Ji; truly relied on Jin and Zheng’s flank-assist blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou looked to the two previous dynasties and enfeoffed the house of Ji, truly blessed by the support of Jin and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖龍興，尊王子弟，大啟九國，卒斬諸呂，以安大宗。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor’s dragon rise honored king sons and younger brothers; greatly opened nine states; in the end beheaded the various Lüs, thereby to settle the great clan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rose like a dragon, honored imperial princes, opened nine kingdoms, and in the end slew the Lü clan to secure the great line.

sentences.zh: 今操惡直醜正，寔繁有徒，包藏禍心，篡盜已顯。

translations.literal: Now Cao hates straightness and uglifies the upright; truly many have followers; harbors misfortune’s heart; usurpation and theft already manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Now Cao Cao hates the upright, numbers his followers beyond count, nurses treason in his breast, and his usurpation stands plain.

sentences.zh: 既宗室微弱，帝族無位，斟酌古式，依假權宜，上臣大司馬漢中王。

translations.literal: Since the imperial clan is feeble and weak, the emperor’s kin lack position, weigh ancient models, rely on borrowed expedient, upward your subject as Grand Marshal King of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial house is weak and princes hold no power; weighing ancient models and present need, they have raised your subject as grand marshal and king of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 臣伏自三省，受國厚恩，荷任一方，陳力未效，所獲已過，不宜复忝高位以重罪謗。

translations.literal: Your subject prostrate self three-reflects; received the state’s thick grace; bears charge of one region; displayed strength without effect; what obtained already passes measure; not fitting again to disgrace high rank thereby to double crime and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject reflects in humility: the state has favored me, I hold a frontier yet have done little, and my rewards already exceed my merit—I should not again shame a high post and invite reproach.

sentences.zh: 群寮見逼，迫臣以義。

translations.literal: The host of colleagues saw and pressed; pressed your subject with righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: My colleagues press me in the name of duty.

sentences.zh: 臣退惟寇賊不梟，國難未已，宗廟傾危，社稷將墜，成臣憂責碎首之負。

translations.literal: Your servant withdrawing considers: bandits not owl-removed; state hardship not yet ended; ancestral temples tilt in peril; altars of soil and grain about to fall—completes your servant’s sorrow-duty, shattered-head’s burden.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I see the rebels still at large, the crisis unended, the temples tottering and the altars about to fall—failure would be my burden to the death.

sentences.zh: 若應權通變，以寧靖聖朝，雖赴水火，所不得辭，敢慮常宜，以防後悔。

translations.literal: If responding to weight and penetrating change thereby to quiet and settle the sage court—although go to water and fire, cannot decline; dare consider common propriety, thereby to guard later regret.
translations.idiomatic: If expedient change can restore the court, I would enter flood or fire without demur—I dare not cling to ordinary scruple and invite later remorse.

sentences.zh: 輒順眾議，拜受印璽，以崇國威。

translations.literal: Rashly followed the host’s counsel, bowed and received seal and jade, thereby to exalt state awe.
translations.idiomatic: I have yielded to their counsel, bowed and received the seals, to magnify the majesty of the state.

sentences.zh: 仰惟爵號，位高寵厚，俯思報效，憂深責重，驚怖累息，如臨於谷。

translations.literal: Looking up consider rank and title, position high favor thick; looking down think repayment, worry deep duty heavy; fear and terror piled sighs; as if standing at a gorge.
translations.idiomatic: I look up at titles so high and favor so deep, look down on the debt I owe, and tremble as if on a cliff’s edge.

sentences.zh: 盡力輸誠，獎厲六師，率齊群義，應天順時，撲討凶逆，以寧社稷，以報萬分，謹拜章因驛上還所假左將軍、宜城亭侯印綬。

translations.literal: Exhaust strength and convey sincerity, encourage six armies, lead and align the host of righteousness, respond to Heaven and obey the season, strike and punish fierce rebels, thereby to quiet the altars of soil and grain, thereby to repay the myriad part; respectfully bow chapter and by relay upward return the lent Left General and Yicheng village marquis seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: I will give my utmost, rouse the six hosts, rally the righteous, obey Heaven’s season, strike the traitors, and secure the altars in repayment beyond measure; I hereby return by courier the seals of left general and marquis of Yicheng village lent me for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 於是還治成都。

translations.literal: Thereupon returned to administer Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned his government to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 拔魏延為都督，鎮漢中。

translations.literal: Raised Wei Yan as area commander, garrisoned Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Wei Yan to area commander to hold Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 〈典略曰：備於是起館舍，築亭障，從成都至白水關，四百餘區。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Compendium says: Bei thereupon raised lodges and houses, built watchtowers and barriers, from Chengdu to Baishui Pass, more than four hundred sections.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Compendium says he built posts and ramparts in more than four hundred sections from Chengdu to Baishui Pass.”

sentences.zh: 時關羽攻曹公將曹仁，禽于禁於樊。

translations.literal: At that time Guan Yu attacked Lord Cao’s general Cao Ren; captured Yu Jin at Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Guan Yu besieged Cao Ren and took Yu Jin prisoner at Fan.

sentences.zh: 俄而孫權襲殺羽，取荊州。

translations.literal: Before long Sun Quan raided and killed Yu, took Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sun Quan struck, killed Guan Yu, and seized Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，魏文帝稱尊號，改年曰黃初。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Wei Emperor Wen assumed honored title; changed the year to Huangchu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Cao Pi of Wei took the imperial title and changed the era name to Huangchu.

sentences.zh: 或傳聞漢帝見害，先主乃發喪制服，追諡曰孝愍皇帝。

translations.literal: Some heard rumor the Han emperor was seen harmed; the Former Lord then issued mourning and donned mourning garments; posthumously titled Filial Compassionate Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that the Han emperor had been murdered; Liu Bei then went into mourning and posthumously titled him Emperor Xiaomin.

sentences.zh: 是後在所並言眾瑞，日月相屬，故議郎陽泉侯劉豹、青衣侯向舉、偏將軍張裔、黃權、大司馬屬殷純、益州別駕從事趙莋、治中從事楊洪、從事祭酒何宗、議曹從事杜瓊、勸學從事張爽、尹默、譙周等上言：

translations.literal: After this in places together spoke many auspices, sun and moon linked in succession; therefore Gentleman-adviser village marquis of Yangquan Liu Bao, village marquis of Qingyi Xiang Ju, major general Zhang Yi, Huang Quan, Grand Marshal’s subordinate Yin Chun, Yizhou chief clerk Zhao Zha, headquarters clerk Yang Hong, clerk libationer He Zong, consult bureau clerk Du Qiong, encourage-learning clerk Zhang Shuang, Yin Mo, Qiao Zhou and others upward spoke:
translations.idiomatic: Thenceforth every district reported omens in endless succession; Gentleman-adviser Liu Bao, marquis of Yangquan, Xiang Ju, marquis of Qingyi, Major General Zhang Yi, Huang Quan, Yin Chun of the grand marshal’s staff, chief clerk Zhao Zha, headquarters clerk Yang Hong, libationer He Zong, Du Qiong of the consult bureau, Zhang Shuang, Yin Mo, Qiao Zhou, and others memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣聞河圖、洛書，五經讖、緯，孔子所甄，驗應自遠。

translations.literal: Your servants have heard the River Chart and Luo Document, the Five Classics' prophecies and weft-texts, what Kongzi selected—verification and response come from afar.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that the River Chart, Luo Writing, and the apocrypha on the Five Classics, which Confucius judged, have borne their signs from of old.

sentences.zh: 謹案洛書甄曜度曰：‘赤三日德昌，九世會備，合為帝際。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the Luo Document Zhenyao Du says: 'Red three days virtue prospers; nine generations meet Bei; together is the emperor's juncture.
translations.idiomatic: The Luo Document Zhenyao Du states: when the red house has flourished three days, the ninth generation will meet Bei—the moment of the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: ’洛書寶號命曰：‘天度帝道備稱皇，以統握契，百成不敗。

translations.literal: ' The Luo Document Baohaoming says: 'Heaven measures the imperial way complete, titled emperor, thereby to grasp the tally—hundred successes, no defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Baohaoming says: when Heaven's measure and the imperial way are complete, he is called emperor, grasps the mandate, and a hundred campaigns do not fail.

sentences.zh: ’洛書錄運期曰：‘九侯七傑爭命民炊骸，道路籍籍履人頭，誰使主者玄且來。

translations.literal: ' The Luo Document Lu Yunqi says: 'Nine marquises seven heroes vie for the mandate; people boil bones; roads noisy treading on men's heads—who makes the ruler dark and yet come.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu Yunqi says: when nine lords and seven champions fight for the mandate and the people boil in misery, who will rule but the dark lord who comes?

sentences.zh: ’孝經鉤命決錄曰：‘帝三建九會備。

translations.literal: ' The Classic of Filial Piety Gouming Juelu says: 'The emperor three establishes nine meets Bei.
translations.idiomatic: The Gouming Juelu on the Classic of Filial Piety says: the emperor thrice establishes the realm; the ninth convergence is Bei.

sentences.zh: ’臣父群未亡時，言西南數有黃氣，直立數丈，見來積年，時時有景雲祥風，從璿璣下來應之，此為異瑞。

translations.literal: ' Your servant's father Qun before he died said: in the southwest repeatedly there was yellow qi, standing straight several rods; seen coming piled years; from time to time there were bright-cloud auspicious winds, from the pivot stars descending in response—this is a strange auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Before my father Chen Qun died he said that for years yellow mists had risen straight from the southwest, bright clouds and lucky winds answered from the pole stars—an extraordinary omen.

sentences.zh: 又二十二年中，數有氣如旗，從西竟東，中天而行，圖、書曰‘必有天子出其方’。

translations.literal: Moreover in the twenty-second year, repeatedly there was qi like a banner, from west to east end, mid-sky moving; charts and books say 'there must be a Son of Heaven emerging from that quarter'.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year a banner-shaped vapor ran from west to east across the sky; the charts say, a Son of Heaven will arise from that direction.

sentences.zh: 加是年太白、熒惑、填星，常從歲星相追。

translations.literal: Add this year Grand White, Sparkling Deluder, Filling Star, constantly followed the Year Star chasing each other.
translations.idiomatic: That year Venus, Mars, and Saturn repeatedly converged on Jupiter.

sentences.zh: 近漢初興，五星從歲星謀；

translations.literal: Near Han's first rise, the five planets followed the Year Star in counsel;
translations.idiomatic: At Han's founding the five planets gathered with Jupiter;

sentences.zh: 歲星主義，漢位在西，義之上方，故漢法常以歲星候人主。

translations.literal: the Year Star governs righteousness; Han's position is in the west, above righteousness's quarter; therefore Han's method always used the Year Star to watch the lord of men.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter governs righteousness; Han's quarter lies in the west above it, so Han astrologers read the ruler in Jupiter.

sentences.zh: 當有聖主起於此州，以致中興。

translations.literal: There ought to be a sage lord rising from this province, thereby to bring middle revival.
translations.idiomatic: A sage ruler should rise from this province to restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 時許帝尚存，故群下不敢漏言。

translations.literal: At that time the Xu emperor still survived; therefore the host below did not dare leak words.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xian still lived, none dared speak openly.

sentences.zh: 頃者熒惑复追歲星，見在胃昴畢；

translations.literal: Recently Sparkling Deluder again pursued the Year Star; seen in Stomach, Hairy Head, Net;
translations.idiomatic: Lately Mars has again pursued Jupiter through the lodges Stomach, Hairy Head, and Net;

sentences.zh: 昴畢為天綱，經曰‘帝星處之，眾邪消亡’。

translations.literal: Hairy Head and Net are Heaven's net; the classic says 'when the emperor star dwells there, the host of evils vanish'.
translations.idiomatic: those lodges are the celestial net; the classic says, when the emperor star stands there, every evil perishes.

sentences.zh: 聖諱豫睹，推揆期驗，符合數至，若此非一。

translations.literal: The sage's taboo-name foreseen; push and measure period verification; tally and fit numbers arrive; like this not one alone.
translations.idiomatic: Your taboo name was foreseen; reckoning the dates, the tallies arrive again and again—not this sign alone.

sentences.zh: 臣聞聖王先天而天不違，後天而奉天時，故應際而生，與神合契。

translations.literal: Your servants have heard the sage king is before Heaven yet Heaven does not oppose; after Heaven yet obeys Heaven's season; therefore responds to the juncture and is born, joins spirits in tally.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that the sage king anticipates Heaven without opposing it, follows Heaven without missing the hour—thus he is born for the moment and matches the gods.

sentences.zh: 原大王應天順民，速即洪業，以寧海內。

translations.literal: We pray the great king respond to Heaven and obey the people, speedily mount the vast enterprise, thereby to quiet within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you, great king, to answer Heaven and the people, take the great enterprise at once, and bring peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 太傅許靖、安漢將軍糜竺、軍師將軍諸葛亮、太常賴恭、光祿勳

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Xu Jing, General Who Pacifies Han Mi Zhu, General of the Army Zhuge Liang, Grand Master of Ceremonies Lai Gong, Superintendent of the Imperial Household
translations.idiomatic: Grand tutor Xu Jing, general who pacifies Han Mi Zhu, general of the army Zhuge Liang, grand master of ceremonies Lai Gong, superintendent of the imperial household

sentences.zh: （黃權）

translations.literal: (Huang Quan [variant])
translations.idiomatic: Some texts read Huang Quan here;

sentences.zh: 〔黃柱〕、少府王謀等上言：

translations.literal: [Huang Zhu], Superintendent of the Privy Treasury Wang Mou and others upward spoke:
translations.idiomatic: [Huang Zhu], superintendent of the privy treasury Wang Mou, and others memorialized:

sentences.zh: 曹丕篡弒，湮滅漢室，竊據神器，劫迫忠良，酷烈無道。

translations.literal: Cao Pi usurped and murdered, extinguished the Han house, stole the sacred vessels, coerced the loyal and good, cruel and lawless without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi usurped and murdered, snuffed out the house of Han, seized the throne, coerced the loyal, and trampled every law.

sentences.zh: 人鬼忿毒，咸思劉氏。

translations.literal: Men and ghosts resent poison; all think on the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Men and spirits alike burn with hate and long for the house of Liu.

sentences.zh: 今上無天子，海內惶惶，靡所式仰。

translations.literal: Now above there is no Son of Heaven; within the seas panic-stricken; none have whom to model and look up to.
translations.idiomatic: There is no emperor above; the realm trembles and has no pole to look to.

sentences.zh: 群下前後上書者八百餘人，咸稱述符瑞，圖、讖明徵。

translations.literal: The host below front and back upward memorialized more than eight hundred persons; all proclaimed and narrated talisman auspices, charts and prophecies clear signs.
translations.idiomatic: More than eight hundred memorials from your officers cite omens, charts, and prophecies as plain proof.

sentences.zh: 間黃龍見武陽赤水，九日乃去。

translations.literal: Meanwhile a yellow dragon appeared at Chishui in Wuyang; nine days then departed.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow dragon appeared at Chishui in Wuyang and stayed nine days.

sentences.zh: 孝經援神契曰‘德至淵泉則黃龍見’，龍者，君之像也。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety Yuanshenqi says 'when virtue reaches the deep springs then the yellow dragon appears'; the dragon is the lord's image.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanshenqi on the Classic of Filial Piety says: when virtue reaches the deep springs, the yellow dragon appears—and the dragon is the image of the ruler.

sentences.zh: 易乾九五‘飛龍在天’，大王當龍昇，登帝位也。

translations.literal: The Changes Qian nine-five 'flying dragon in the sky'—the great king ought dragon ascend, mount the emperor's position.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes, Qian's fifth line, says the flying dragon is in the sky—the great king should mount the throne.

sentences.zh: 又前關羽圍樊、襄陽，襄陽男子張嘉、王休獻玉璽，璽潛漢水，伏於淵泉，暉景燭燿，靈光徹天。

translations.literal: Moreover earlier when Guan Yu besieged Fan and Xiangyang, Xiangyang men Zhang Jia and Wang Xiu presented a jade seal; the seal sank in Han water, hid in the deep spring; radiance gleamed and spiritual light pierced Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Guan Yu besieged Fan and Xiangyang, Zhang Jia and Wang Xiu of Xiangyang offered a jade seal that sank into the Han, glowed from the depths, and lit the sky.

sentences.zh: 夫漢者，高祖本所起定天下之國號也，大王襲先帝軌跡，亦興於漢中也。

translations.literal: Now Han is the dynastic name Gaozu originally rose to settle the realm; the great king inherits the former emperor's tracks, also rose in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Han is the name Gaozu took when he won the realm; you, great king, follow the former emperors' path and likewise rose from Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 今天子玉璽神光先見，璽出襄陽，漢水之末，明大王承其下流，授與大王以天子之位，瑞命符應，非人力所致。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven's jade seal divine light first appeared; the seal came out of Xiangyang, at Han water's end—makes clear the great king receives its lower flow, is given the Son of Heaven's position; auspicious mandate tally responds—not human power brought about.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial seal's light appeared first; the seal emerged at Xiangyang on the lower Han—showing that you receive its current and Heaven's mandate, not human contrivance.

sentences.zh: 昔周有烏魚之瑞，咸曰休哉。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou had crow and fish auspices; all said how excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had omens of crows and fish; all cried excellent.

sentences.zh: 二祖受命，圖、書先著，以為徵驗。

translations.literal: The two ancestors received the mandate; charts and books first set forth, taken as verification.
translations.idiomatic: The two founding emperors received Heaven's charge with charts and books foretelling it.

sentences.zh: 今上天告祥，群儒英俊，並進河、洛，孔子讖、記，咸悉具至。

translations.literal: Now Heaven above announces auspices; the host of scholars and heroes together advance River and Luo, Kongzi's prophecies and records—all fully arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends auspices; scholars and worthies cite the River and Luo texts and Confucian prophecies in full.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大王出自孝景皇帝中山靖王之冑，本支百世，乾祇降祚，聖姿碩茂，神武在躬，仁覆積德，愛人好士，是以四方歸心焉。

translations.literal: We prostrate ourselves: the great king comes from Emperor Xiaojing's Prince Jing of Zhongshan; root and branch a hundred generations; Qian and earth spirits send blessing; sage form great and lush; divine martial in the person; benevolence covering piled virtue; loves men and esteems knights—therefore the four quarters' hearts return.
translations.idiomatic: You descend from Emperor Jing's Prince Jing of Zhongshan; your line runs a hundred generations; Heaven and earth bless you; your form is majestic, your might godlike, your virtue deep; you love men and honor scholars—so the realm turns to you.

sentences.zh: 考省靈圖，啟發讖、緯，神明之表，名諱昭著。

translations.literal: Examining the spirit charts, opening and issuing prophecies and weft-texts, the divine surface, taboo name clearly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit charts and apocrypha show your name plain as day.

sentences.zh: 宜即帝位，以纂二祖，紹嗣昭穆，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Ought immediately to mount the emperor's position, thereby to continue the two ancestors, continue the bright-altar order; all under Heaven greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: You should take the throne, continue the two Han founders, and set the temple order right—great fortune for the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹與博士許慈、議郎孟光，建立禮儀，擇令辰，上尊號。

translations.literal: We respectfully with erudite Xu Ci, Gentleman-adviser Meng Guang, established ritual and ceremony, chose an auspicious day, upward presented the honored title.
translations.idiomatic: We have drawn up the rites with Erudite Xu Ci and Gentleman-adviser Meng Guang, chosen an auspicious day, and present the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 即皇帝位於成都武擔之南。

translations.literal: Immediately mounted the emperor's position south of Wudan in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He took the imperial title south of Wudan Mound in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 〈蜀本紀曰：武都有丈夫化為女子，顏色美好，蓋山精也。

translations.literal: The Shu Basic Annals says: in Wudu a husband changed into a woman, countenance fair and good—probably a mountain sprite.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Basic Annals says a man of Wudu turned into a woman of ravishing beauty—a mountain spirit.

sentences.zh: 蜀王娶以為妻，不習水土，疾病欲歸國，蜀王留之，無幾物故。

translations.literal: The king of Shu took her as wife; she did not acclimate to soil and water, fell ill and wished to return to her state; the king of Shu detained her; before long she died.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Shu married her; she sickened in the climate and begged to leave; he kept her until she died.

sentences.zh: 蜀王發卒之武都擔土，於成都郭中葬，蓋地數畝，高十丈，號曰武擔也。

translations.literal: The king of Shu sent soldiers to Wudu to shoulder earth, in Chengdu's outer wall buried her, covering several mu of ground, height ten zhang, called Wudan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to Wudu to carry earth and buried her inside Chengdu's wall in a mound several mu wide and ten zhang high called Wudan.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：武擔，山名，在成都西北，蓋以乾位在西北，故就之以即阼。〉

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi's note: Wudan is a mountain name, northwest of Chengdu—probably because the Qian position is northwest, therefore approached it to mount the steps.>
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Wudan is a hill northwest of Chengdu; the Qian trigram lies in the northwest, so the rite faced it for accession.

sentences.zh: 為文曰：

translations.literal: Made a text saying:
translations.idiomatic: The proclamation read:

sentences.zh: 惟建安二十六年四月丙午，皇帝備敢用玄牡，昭告皇天上帝后土神祇：漢有天下，歷數無疆。

translations.literal: Only the twenty-sixth year of Jian'an, fourth month bingwu day, Emperor Bei dares use black male victims, clearly announce August Heaven High God and later earth spirits: Han possesses the realm, its reckoning without limit.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu in the fourth month of the twenty-sixth year of Jian'an, the emperor Bei offers black victims and announces to August Heaven, High God, and the spirits of earth: Han holds the mandate without end.

sentences.zh: 曩者王莽篡盜，光武皇帝震怒致誅，社稷復存。

translations.literal: Formerly Wang Mang usurped and stole; Emperor Guangwu roused in wrath and punished; the altars of soil and grain again survived.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang once usurped the throne; Emperor Guangwu rose in wrath and restored the altars.

sentences.zh: 今曹操阻兵安忍，戮殺主後，滔天泯夏，罔顧天顯。

translations.literal: Now Cao Cao blocks troops and rests in cruelty, slaughtered empress and heir, floods Heaven and extinguished summer, disregards Heaven's manifest will.
translations.idiomatic: Now Cao Cao arms himself in cruelty, slew empress and crown prince, defies Heaven, and scorns the bright mandate.

sentences.zh: 操子丕，載其凶逆，竊居神器。

translations.literal: Cao's son Pi, carries his fierce rebellion, secretly occupies the sacred vessels.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pi carries on that villainy and steals the throne.

sentences.zh: 群臣將士以為社稷墮廢，備宜脩之，嗣武二祖，龔行天罰。

translations.literal: The host of ministers and generals consider the altars of soil and grain fallen and ruined; Bei ought to repair them, continue martial of the two ancestors, respectfully enact Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers hold that the altars have fallen and that you must restore them, continue the martial virtue of the two founders, and carry out Heaven's punishment.

sentences.zh: 備惟否德，懼忝帝位。

translations.literal: Bei alone considers his lacking virtue, fears disgracing the emperor's seat.
translations.idiomatic: I know my virtue is slight and fear to shame the throne.

sentences.zh: 詢於庶民，外及蠻夷君長，僉曰‘天命不可以不答，祖業不可以久替，四海不可以無主’ 。

translations.literal: Consulted the common people, outward reaching to barbarian chiefs; all said 'Heaven's mandate cannot go unanswered, ancestral enterprise cannot long be replaced, within the four seas cannot lack a lord'.
translations.idiomatic: I asked the people and the barbarian chiefs; all said the mandate cannot be refused, the ancestral work cannot lapse, and the realm cannot lack a ruler.

sentences.zh: 率土式望，在備一人。

translations.literal: All within the soil look up in hope—in Bei alone.
translations.idiomatic: The realm looks to me alone.

sentences.zh: 備畏天明命，又懼漢阼將湮於地，謹擇元日，與百寮登壇，受皇帝璽綬。

translations.literal: Bei fears bright Heaven's mandate, and fears the Han throne will sink into earth; respectfully chose the first day, with the hundred officials ascended the altar, received the emperor's seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: I fear Heaven's command and the fall of Han; I have chosen an auspicious day, ascended the altar with the hundred officials, and received the imperial seal and ribbon.

sentences.zh: 脩燔瘞，告類於天神，惟神饗祚於漢家，永綏四海！

translations.literal: Performed burning and burying sacrifices, reported category to Heaven's spirits; only may the spirits feast blessing on the house of Han, forever pacify the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: I have offered the burnt and buried sacrifices and told Heaven: may you bless the house of Han and forever quiet the seas!

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，先主軍還秭歸，將軍吳班、陳式水軍屯夷陵，夾江東西岸。

translations.literal: Second year spring first month, the Former Lord's army returned to Zigui; generals Wu Ban and Chen Shi water army garrisoned Yiling, flanking the river east and west banks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Zhangwu he withdrew to Zigui; Wu Ban and Chen Shi camped the fleet at Yiling on both banks of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 二月，先主自秭歸率諸將進軍，緣山截嶺，於夷道猇亭

translations.literal: Second month, the Former Lord from Zigui led the various generals advancing the army, along mountains cutting ridges, at Yidao Xiaoting
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he led his generals from Zigui over the ridges to Xiaoting at Yidao,

sentences.zh: 〈猇，許交反。〉

translations.literal: <Xiao read like xiao in entering tone.>
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: read xiao in the entering tone.

sentences.zh: 駐營，自佷山

translations.literal: encamped, from Hen Mountain
translations.idiomatic: He camped there and advanced from Hen Mountain

sentences.zh: 〈佷，音恆。〉

translations.literal: <Hen read like heng.>
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: Hen is read like heng.

sentences.zh: 通武陵，遣侍中馬良安慰五谿蠻夷，咸相率響應。

translations.literal: opened passage to Wuling; sent Palace Attendant Ma Liang to console the five gorges barbarians; all together led and responded.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a route to Wuling and sent Ma Liang to reassure the five-streams tribes, who rallied in answer.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍黃權督江北諸軍，與吳軍相拒於夷陵道。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the North Huang Quan supervised north-of-the-river various armies, with Wu's army faced each other at Yiling road.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan, general who guards the north, commanded the troops north of the river against Wu on the Yiling road.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，黃氣見自秭歸十餘里中，廣數十丈。

translations.literal: Summer sixth month, yellow qi appeared from Zigui more than ten li within, breadth several tens of rods.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month yellow mist rose for more than ten li around Zigui, dozens of yards wide.

sentences.zh: 後十餘日，陸議大破先主軍於猇亭，將軍馮習、張南等皆沒。

translations.literal: After more than ten days, Lu Yi greatly broke the Former Lord's army at Xiaoting; generals Feng Xi, Zhang Nan and others all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Lu Xun shattered Liu Bei's army at Xiaoting; Feng Xi, Zhang Nan, and others fell.

sentences.zh: 先主自猇亭還秭歸，收合離散兵，遂棄船舫，由步道還魚复，改魚复縣曰永安。

translations.literal: The Former Lord from Xiaoting returned to Zigui, gathered and combined scattered troops, then cast away boats and barges, by foot path returned to Yufu, changed Yufu county's name to Yongan.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back from Xiaoting to Zigui, rallied stragglers, abandoned the ships, marched overland to Yufu, and renamed the county Yongan.

sentences.zh: 吳遣將軍李異、劉阿等踵躡先主軍，屯駐南山。

translations.literal: Wu sent generals Li Yi, Liu A and others treading on the Former Lord's army, encamped stationed on South Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent Li Yi and Liu A to dog his heels and camp on South Mountain.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，收兵還巫。

translations.literal: Autumn eighth month, gathered troops returned to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he withdrew to Wu county.

sentences.zh: 司徒許靖卒。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Xu Jing died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jing, minister of education, died.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，詔丞相亮營南北郊於成都。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, edict Chancellor Liang to arrange south and north suburban altars at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he ordered Zhuge Liang to set up the suburban altars at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 孫權聞先主住白帝，甚懼，遣使請和。

translations.literal: Sun Quan heard the Former Lord lodged at Baidi, greatly feared, sent envoys requesting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan, alarmed that Liu Bei was at Baidi, sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 先主許之，遣太中大夫宗瑋報命。

translations.literal: The Former Lord permitted it; sent Grand Palace Grandee Zong Wei to return answer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei agreed and sent Zong Wei with the reply.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，漢嘉太守黃元聞先主疾不豫，舉兵拒守。

translations.literal: Winter twelfth month, Hanjia grand administrator Huang Yuan heard the Former Lord's illness was not well, raised troops to resist and guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Huang Yuan, grand administrator of Hanjia, heard Liu Bei was failing and rose in arms.

sentences.zh: 三年春二月，丞相亮自成都到永安。

translations.literal: Third year spring second month, Chancellor Liang from Chengdu arrived at Yongan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year Zhuge Liang came from Chengdu to Yongan.

sentences.zh: 三月，黃元進兵攻臨邛縣。

translations.literal: Third month, Huang Yuan advanced troops to attack Linqiang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Huang Yuan marched on Linqiang.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍陳曶

translations.literal: Sent General Chen Hu
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Chen Hu

sentences.zh: 〈音笏。〉

translations.literal: <Read like hu.>
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: read like hu.

sentences.zh: 討元，元軍敗，順流下江，為其親兵所縛，生致成都，斬之。

translations.literal: to punish Yuan; Yuan's army was defeated, followed the current down the river, was bound by his personal troops, alive delivered to Chengdu, beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hu attacked him; Huang Yuan was routed, fled downriver, was seized by his own guard, brought alive to Chengdu, and executed.

sentences.zh: 先主病篤，託孤於丞相亮，尚書令李嚴為副。

translations.literal: The Former Lord was critically ill, entrusted the orphan to Chancellor Liang, Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Yan as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he entrusted his heir to Zhuge Liang with Li Yan as second.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸巳，先主殂於永安宮，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month guisi day, the Former Lord died at Yongan Palace; at the time age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi in the fourth month he died in Yongan Palace at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 〈諸葛亮集載先主遺詔敕後主曰：

translations.literal: The Collected Works of Zhuge Liang records the Former Lord's testament edict instructing the Later Lord, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Collected Works of Zhuge Liang preserves the Former Lord's deathbed edict to the heir, which reads:

sentences.zh: 朕初疾但下痢耳，後轉雜他病，殆不自濟。

translations.literal: When I first fell ill it was only dysentery in the lower body; afterward it turned mixed with other diseases, almost unable to save myself.
translations.idiomatic: At first my illness was nothing but flux; then other ailments piled in, and I could barely hold on.

sentences.zh: 人五十不稱夭，年已六十有餘，何所复恨，不復自傷，但以卿兄弟為念。

translations.literal: For a man fifty is not called untimely death; my years already exceed sixty; what further to regret; no longer harm myself; only take you elder-younger brothers as thought.
translations.idiomatic: A man past fifty is not counted as dying young; I am past sixty, so what is there to regret? I grieve no longer for myself—only you, my sons, are on my mind.

sentences.zh: 射君到，說丞相嘆卿智量，甚大增脩，過於所望，審能如此，吾復何憂！

translations.literal: Lord She arrived, spoke that the chancellor sighed over your wisdom and capacity, greatly increased and cultivated, exceeding what was hoped; truly able thus, what more do I worry!
translations.idiomatic: When She Jun came, he told me the chancellor praised your mind and judgment—you have grown far beyond what I hoped. If you truly keep to this path, what have I left to fear?

sentences.zh: 勉之，勉之！

translations.literal: Strive, strive!
translations.idiomatic: Strive—strive hard!

sentences.zh: 勿以惡小而為之，勿以善小而不為。

translations.literal: Do not because evil is small do it; do not because good is small not do it.
translations.idiomatic: Do not commit a wrong because it is small, and do not leave a right undone because it is small.

sentences.zh: 惟賢惟德，能服於人。

translations.literal: Only worthy, only virtuous—able to make people submit.
translations.idiomatic: Only worthiness and virtue can win the hearts of others.

sentences.zh: 汝父德薄，勿效之。

translations.literal: Your father's virtue is thin; do not imitate it.
translations.idiomatic: Your father's virtue was slight—do not take after me.

sentences.zh: 可讀漢書、禮記，間暇歷觀諸子及六韜、商君書，益人意智。

translations.literal: May read Han Documents and Record of Rites; in leisure spaningly view the various masters and Six Secret Teachings, Lord Shang's book—they benefit people's intent and wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Read the Book of Han and the Record of Rites; when you have time, browse the masters, the Six Secret Teachings, and the Book of Lord Shang—they sharpen the mind.

sentences.zh: 聞丞相為寫申、韓、管子、六韜一通已畢，未送，道亡，可自更求聞達。

translations.literal: Heard the chancellor for you wrote Shen, Han, Guanzi, Six Secret Teachings one complete set finished, not yet sent, on the road lost; may yourself further seek renown and penetration.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the chancellor copied out for you the Shenzi and Hanfeizi, the Guanzi, and the Six Secret Teachings as a complete set, but it never reached you—lost on the way. See that you pursue learning and make a name for yourself.

sentences.zh: 臨終時，呼魯王與語：「吾亡之後，汝兄弟父事丞相，令卿與丞相共事而已。」〉

translations.literal: At dying time, called the Prince of Lu and spoke with him: 'After my death, you brothers father-serve the chancellor, only let you with the chancellor jointly handle affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: As he lay dying he summoned the Prince of Lu and said: "When I am gone, you brothers are to treat the chancellor as a father; you are simply to work with him in governing."

sentences.zh: 亮上言於後主曰：

translations.literal: Liang upward spoke to the Later Lord, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang memorialized the Later Lord:

sentences.zh: 伏惟大行皇帝邁仁樹德，覆燾無疆，昊天不弔，寢疾彌留，今月二十四日奄忽升遐，臣妾號咷，若喪考妣。
