translations.literal: I prostrate and consider the great-course emperor practiced benevolence planted virtue, covering warming without border; august Heaven does not pity, lying ill lingering; this month's twenty-fourth day suddenly ascended distant; ministers and concubines wail, as if mourning father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor walked in benevolence and planted deep virtue; his kindness sheltered all without limit. Yet August Heaven was unkind: illness held him, and on the twenty-fourth of this month he passed away in a breath. Your ministers and your ladies weep as for a father and mother.

sentences.zh: 乃顧遺詔，事惟大宗，動容損益；

translations.literal: Then turned to testament edict, affairs only great heir, moving countenance harm-benefit;
translations.idiomatic: The testament addresses the great succession and sets every detail of mourning and restraint;

sentences.zh: 百寮發哀，滿三日除服，到葬期復如禮；

translations.literal: Hundred officials express mourning, full three days remove garments, arrive burial period again according ritual;
translations.idiomatic: the hundred officials may mourn three full days, then lay aside mourning dress until the burial, when the full rites resume;

sentences.zh: 其郡國太守、相、都尉、縣令長，三日便除服。

translations.literal: As for commandery-state grand administrators, chancellors, commandants, county magistrates and chiefs, three days then remove mourning.
translations.idiomatic: for commandery and kingdom grand administrators, chancellors, commandants, magistrates, and chiefs, mourning ends after three days.

sentences.zh: 臣亮親受敕戒，震畏神靈，不敢有違。

translations.literal: Your subject Liang personally received edict admonition, trembling fearing spirits, dare not have disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Liang received the edict in person and trembles before the spirits—I dare not disregard it.

sentences.zh: 臣請宣下奉行。

translations.literal: Your subject requests proclaim below and carry out.
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to promulgate it below for compliance.

sentences.zh: 五月，梓宮自永安還成都，諡曰昭烈皇帝。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the cypress palace-coffin from Yongan returned Chengdu, posthumous title said Shining Fierce emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the late emperor's bier was brought from Yongan to Chengdu, and he received the posthumous title Emperor Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，葬惠陵。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, buried at Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he was laid to rest at Huiling.

sentences.zh: 〈葛洪《神仙傳》曰：仙人李意其，蜀人也。

translations.literal: Ge Hong's Traditions of Spirit Immortals says: immortal Li Yiqi, Shu person.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong's Traditions of Divine Transcendents names the immortal Li Yiqi, a man of Shu.

sentences.zh: 傳世見之，雲是漢文帝時人。

translations.literal: Passed generations see him, cloud is Han Wendi era person.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages record him, saying he lived in the time of Emperor Wen of Han.

sentences.zh: 先主欲伐吳，遣人迎意其。

translations.literal: Former Lord wished to attack Wu, dispatched men welcome Yiqi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Lord was about to campaign against Wu, he sent to bring Li Yiqi in.

sentences.zh: 意其到，先主禮敬之，問以吉凶。

translations.literal: Yiqi arrived, Former Lord ritually respected him, asked by auspicious inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiqi came, and the Former Lord received him with full courtesy and asked his fortune.

sentences.zh: 意其不答而求紙筆，畫作兵馬器仗數十紙已，便一一以手裂壞之，又畫作一大人，掘地埋之，便徑去。

translations.literal: Yiqi did not answer but sought paper brush, drew as military horses weapons staves several tens sheets finished, then one by one with hand tore destroyed them, also drew as one great man, dug earth buried it, then straight departed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiqi gave no word but asked for paper and brush. He sketched ranks of men, horses, and arms across dozens of sheets, then tore each drawing to scraps. Next he drew a tall figure, dug a hole, buried the picture, and walked straight out.

sentences.zh: 先主大不喜。

translations.literal: Former Lord greatly not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 而自出軍徵吳，大敗還，忿恥發病死，眾人乃知其意。

translations.literal: But himself went out army campaign Wu, great defeat returned, rage shame arose illness died, crowd people then knew his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he led the army against Wu himself, suffered a crushing defeat, and died of rage and shame—only then did people grasp what Li Yiqi had meant.

sentences.zh: 其畫作大人而埋之者，即是言先主死意。〉

translations.literal: That drew as great man and buried it, namely is saying Former Lord death intent.
translations.idiomatic: The tall figure he buried had foretold the Former Lord's death.

translations.literal: Section label: evaluative commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Evaluative commentary (section heading).

sentences.zh: 評曰：先主之弘毅寬厚，知人待士，蓋有高祖之風，英雄之器焉。

translations.literal: Comment says: Former Lord's magnanimity firmness breadth generosity, knowing people treating knights, probably had Gaozu's wind, hero's vessel therein.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary states: the Former Lord's fortitude, breadth, and warmth, his eye for men and care for retainers, indeed carried something of Gaozu's style and the bearing of a true champion.

sentences.zh: 及其舉國託孤於諸葛亮，而心神無貳，誠君臣之至公，古今之盛軌也。

translations.literal: Reaching his raising whole state entrusting orphan to Zhuge Liang, yet mind spirit no twofold, truly lord-minister's utmost public, ancient-modern's splendid track.
translations.idiomatic: When he placed the whole realm and his son in Zhuge Liang's hands with never a flicker of mistrust, he and his minister reached the height of mutual good faith—a model for all ages.

sentences.zh: 機權幹略，不逮魏武，是以基宇亦狹。

translations.literal: Opportunity power capacity strategy, not reach Wei Wu, therefore foundation roof also narrow.
translations.idiomatic: In shrewdness, power, and strategic grasp he fell short of the Wei ruler, so his foundations remained narrower.

sentences.zh: 然折而不撓，終不為下者，抑揆彼之量必不容己，非唯競利，且以避害云爾。

translations.literal: Yet bent yet not crooked, end not be below one, suppress measure that one's capacity certainly not contain self, not only compete profit, also thereby avoid harm cloud thus.
translations.idiomatic: Yet broken he did not bend, and he would never serve another's rule: weighing Cao Cao's measure, he knew there was no room for him—not only to vie for advantage, but to escape ruin as well.
